data.title: C++ to Rust Phrasebook
data.author: wcrichton
data.article_summary: 《C++ to Rust Phrasebook》是一本帮助C++程序员学习Rust的书，提供了常见C++模式到Rust习惯用法的转换，通过具体代码示例和工程权衡的高层次讨论进行讲解。本书支持随机访问，适合在编写Rust代码时遇到困惑的情况下查阅。由布朗大学认知工程实验室的专家编写，确保信息的准确性和适度细节，所有内容均为人工撰写，无AI生成。适合有一定Rust基础的读者，也可以作为嵌入式系统程序员的补充资料。读者可以提交反馈或参与问卷调查，帮助改进书籍内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C++与Rust语言的对比及其实践差异

不同观点：
• jpc0认为该指南低估了C++的能力，尤其是在枚举、模块等特性上。他指出，C++通过一些编译器标志和现代工具链也能实现类似Rust的功能，而指南忽视了这些。他还提到Rust的FFI（外部函数接口）在处理图形和FFmpeg等特定领域时不如直接用C++方便。
• EliRivers指出，将一种语言的惯用模式应用于另一种语言可能会导致问题。他以C程序员在C++中使用init()函数为例，说明C程序员需要适应C++的构造函数模式。他还提出，C++程序员在写Rust时需要注意哪些“惯用模式”可能不适用。
• gtani推荐了Drysdale的《Effective Rust》一书，认为它也是针对类似受众的优秀资源。
• amelius观察到Rust版本的代码通常更冗长。
• Animats指出，Rust的traits和C++的类有重大区别，尤其是Rust的traits没有关联数据，也无法访问父trait的数据，这会导致面向对象编程变得混乱。他还提到Rust的所有权模型和错误处理方式与C++显著不同。
• npalli认为，反过来看，这个指南可以帮助C++程序员学习Rust的优点，从而改进C++代码。
• unvalley表示，该指南对没有C++经验的Rust开发者也很有帮助。
• 90s_dev计划利用该指南同时学习Rust和C++，以比较两者的优劣。
• leoh对该指南表示高度赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是C++和Rust在某些特性上的实现和便捷性比较。jpc0认为C++被低估，而Rust在某些方面并不如指南所暗示的那样优越。
• 另一个值得注意的点是Rust的所有权模型和错误处理方式，这些是与C++显著不同的核心概念，可能对习惯C++的开发者构成挑战。
• 不同开发者对指南的用途有不同看法，有人用来学习两种语言，有人用来改进自己对某一种语言的使用。

44140349.article_content:
C++ to Rust Phrasebook
This book is designed to help C++ programmers learn Rust. It provides translations of common C++ patterns into idiomatic Rust. Each pattern is described through concrete code examples along with high-level discussion of engineering trade-offs.
The book can be read front-to-back, but it is designed to be used random-access.
When you are writing Rust code and think, "I know how to do this in C++ but not Rust," then
look for the corresponding chapter in this book.
This book was hand-written by expert C++ and Rust programmers at Brown University's
Cognitive Engineering Lab
. Our goal is provide accurate information with a tasteful degree of detail. No text in this book was written by AI.
If you would like updates on when we add new chapters to this book, you can
drop your email here
.
Other resources
If you have zero Rust experience, you might consider first reading
The Rust Programming
Language
or getting a quick overview at
Learn X in Y Minutes
.
If you are primarily an embedded systems programmer using C or C++, this book is
a complement to
The Embedded Rust Book
.
Compared to resources like the
Rustonomicon
and
Learn Rust With Entirely Too Many Linked Lists
, this book is less about "Rust behind the scenes" and more about explicitly describing how Rust works in terms of C++.
Feedback on this book
At the bottom of every page there is a link
to a form where you can submit feedback: typos, factual errors, or any other issues you spot.
If you answer the quizzes at the end of each chapter, we will save your
responses anonymously for research purposes.
Click here to leave us feedback about this page.

data.title: The Illusion of Causality in Charts
data.author: skadamat
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图表与因果错觉之间的关系，以及图表可能导致的误解

不同观点：
• gcanyon认为，文章更多讨论的是潜在的因果关系问题，而非图表在误导方面的具体角色。他指出，散点图本身并没有误导性，它只是展示了数据之间的关系，而误解来源于混杂因素（confounding factors）可能导致的数据误读。他希望文章能更多探讨不同类型的图表如何更容易被误解或更具误导性。

• JackSlateur通过提供一个关于虚假相关的链接，暗示图表可能会展示出误导性的相关性，从而让人错误地推导出因果关系。

• nwlotz强调了《如何用统计撒谎》一书的影响，并表达了对信息过载和AI生成图表可能导致的误导性信息的担忧。他担心这些误导性图表会被用作政策制定的依据。

• djoldman认为问题的根源不在于图表本身，而在于人们对图表的解读。他指出，人类天生不善于质疑数据可视化，且容易发现和追随模式。他建议避免使用“因果”相关的词汇，因为这些词汇往往被滥用且容易引起误解。

• justonceokay提出了“统计束缚”谬误的问题，指出将群体统计数据用于描述个体情况是一种误导。他通过举例说明，个体情况可能与群体统计数据有很大差异，且因果关系的方向是从个体到群体，而非相反。

• NoTranslationL分享了一个实际应用中的问题，即在分析个人数据时，人们容易从图表和相关性中得出错误结论。他们的应用Reflect增加了一个实验功能，以帮助用户形成假设并识别混杂变量，从而避免得出错误结论。

• singularity2001指出，因果关系是一个复杂的数学概念，只有极少数人真正理解，但每个人都经常谈论和“使用”它。他强调，虽然人们对因果关系有直觉，但区分相关性和因果关系的细节往往让人困惑。

补充讨论：
• qixv以一种讽刺的方式评论说，混淆相关性和因果关系的人最终都会死去，暗示这种误解可能会带来严重后果。

总体而言，讨论围绕图表在展示数据和潜在因果关系时的角色，以及人们在解读这些图表时容易犯的错误。争议的焦点在于图表本身的误导性与人们解读错误之间的关系，以及如何在实际应用中避免这些误解。

data.title: Show HN: PunchCard Key Backup
data.author: ciprian_craciun
data.article_summary: 该项目名为“punchcard-key-backup”，旨在通过打孔卡的方式将128位信息备份到物理介质中。用户可以通过项目网页输入或随机生成128位数据，获得打孔图案，并使用铝片、打孔工具等简单工具制作备份卡片。恢复数据时，只需根据卡片上的孔洞图案在网页上选择对应选项，即可还原原始数据。项目提供自包含的HTML文件，不依赖外部资源，所有资源嵌入HTML中。用户也可以通过Python脚本手动生成和恢复数据。该方法不提供冗余，但使用坚固材料如不锈钢可增强耐久性。项目代码和文档采用CC BY 4.0许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过打孔金属板存储加密信息的方案及其优缺点

不同观点：
• [im_down_w_otp] 表示非常喜欢这个方案，并计划将其应用于自己的数控 router，以便按需生成这些金属板。
• [yencabulator] 推荐了一个相关项目 "paperback"，并提供了一个视频链接，供参考。
• [cypherpunks01] 提出使用更密集的256位卡存储完整年龄密钥，并通过金属钥匙非对称加密任意数量的数据，同时建议使用 "sops" 进行阈值处理，以实现 M of N 备份解密。
• [neilv] 欣赏方案的生存能力和手工工具可行性，但建议使用数字和字母印章或激光切割以提高信息密度和可读性。
• [rubyfan] 联想到军队中使用的非长期保存的纸条钥匙，可以像任务 impossible 一样焚烧。
• [G_o_D] 提出通过刷漆或暗房技术打印孔洞，并建议通过分割金属板或叠加掩码板实现更复杂的加密方法。
• [QuadrupleA] 质疑是否打印QR码更简单，并认为如果只是为了复古趣味可以继续。
• [throwanem] 提醒注意存储环境的电化学影响，建议避免不同金属接触等问题。
• [kens] 质疑128位的容量，期望打孔卡能容纳更多信息。
• [kristianp] 欣赏方案的Python代码简洁性，并提供了一个示例。
• [noman-land] 提到Cryptosteel作为类似产品，但未被其他人提及。
• [thih9] 担心长时间后会忘记解码方法，建议直接雕刻常规字符更简单。
• [Mraedis] 觉得方案愚蠢但有趣，个人更倾向于直接在石板上打印文字。
• [msk-lywenn] 认为这个方案像新的二维条码，质疑为何不直接使用有冗余的QR码。
• [deadbabe] 建议开发一个用户界面，以便更快输入1和0，而不是点击复选框。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：方案的实用性与复杂性之间的平衡。部分人认为直接使用现有技术如QR码更简单，而其他人则欣赏方案的创意和手工操作的趣味。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：包括存储环境的考虑、信息密度和可读性的提升、以及不同加密方法的实现和安全性讨论。

pckb -- PunchCard Key Backup
About
This small project
-- available live at
https://volution.ro/pckb
(or
https://purl.org/999
for long term permanence)
-- allows one to take any 128 bits of information,
and easily create
(
and especially easily recover
)
a backup of it into a physical medium,
by using the old and tried method of
punched cards
(hence the project's name).
For example,
the 128 bit number represented in hexadecimal as
d74ae47dc6f599d3f9cb847bd77d6b7c
,
can be backed up as the following standard (CR80 ID) card sized aluminium sheet,
which can then be put into a safe place:
All of this can be achieved by anyone at home, with access only to the following:
using the self-contained HTML at the link above (
https://volution.ro/pckb
),
either by entering the data manually, or by generating random data,
one can get the hole punching pattern;
(this whole procedure is described in the
help
,
and you could consult it for more details;)
from the same link above, or from
here
,
one can print a standard (CR80 ID) card sized stencil,
to be used as a guide for the hole punching;
a small sheet of aluminium;
(I've used a 0.5mm thick one I've bought from the hardware store for ~4 EUR;)
a
punch tool
,
used to mark (with the help of the stencil)
where the holes should be punched;
a small drill,
used to actually punch the holes;
(I've used a 1.00mm drill bit adapted to a standard screwdriver;)
a cutter, to cut the aluminium steel sheet to the standard (CR80 ID) card size;
(I've just used a ruler, and passed the cutter multiple times over the aluminium sheet,
and in the end, it passed through;)
(obviously, one can just use a wood plank, nail, and rock;)  :)
The recovery is as simple as:
use the same self-contained HTML at the link above;
make sure the checkboxes follow the punched holes pattern (for the key);
check that the CRC checkboxes match the punched holes pattern (for the CRC);
recover the base 10, hexadecimal, or text representation of the backendup information;
Alternatively, without any software,
just use simple binary to decimal (or other base) conversion as described
on Wikipedia
.
FAQ (Frequently asked questions)
How can I trust the HTML you've provided?
You can (and should) save it locally, and use it from your computer.
It doesn't load any external resources.
None;  even the images and attachments are saved as
data:
URIs,
thus embedded into the HTML itself.
Do I even need the HTML you've provided?
You don't.
This is just one possible implementation,
mainly meant for experimentation.
You can easily just write the following snippet to generate the bit pattern:
python -c '_secret = "d74ae47dc6f599d3f9cb847bd77d6b7c" ; print (bin(int(_secret,16))[2:])'
And, for the reverse just write the following snippet:
python -c '_bits = "11010111010010101110010001111101110001101111010110011001110100111111100111001011100001000111101111010111011111010110101101111100" ; print (("%032x"%int(_bits,2)))'
What if I have more than 128 bits to save?
Use a cryptographic tool such as
https://github.com/FiloSottile/age
or
https://github.com/gpg/gnupg
to encrypt your secret data with a random 128 bit password (encoded into hexadecimal),
then backup the password as described above (by using the
key hex
input field),
and mirror your encrypted data to family and friends.
How much redundancy is there in the resulting backup?
None, besides the 16 bits of CRC.
However,
by using sturdy materials
(such as a thick stainless steel sheet),
there shouldn't be much need for redundancy.
Does it support secret sharing?
This is in fact, just a digital-to-physical-medium encoding scheme,
thus with enough imagination, it can support secret sharing.
See the Wikipedia page about
secret sharing
for possible ideas.

• [yencabulator] 推荐了一个相关项目 "paperback"，并提供了一个视频链接，供参考。
• [cypherpunks01] 提出使用更密集的256位卡存储完整年龄密钥，并通过金属钥匙非对称加密任意数量的数据，同时建议使用 "sops" 进行阈值处理，以实现 M of N 备份解密。
• [neilv] 欣赏方案的生存能力和手工工具可行性，但建议使用数字和字母印章或激光切割以提高信息密度和可读性。
• [rubyfan] 联想到军队中使用的非长期保存的纸条钥匙，可以像任务 impossible 一样焚烧。
• [G_o_D] 提出通过刷漆或暗房技术打印孔洞，并建议通过分割金属板或叠加掩码板实现更复杂的加密方法。
• [QuadrupleA] 质疑是否打印QR码更简单，并认为如果只是为了复古趣味可以继续。
• [throwanem] 提醒注意存储环境的电化学影响，建议避免不同金属接触等问题。
• [kens] 质疑128位的容量，期望打孔卡能容纳更多信息。
• [kristianp] 欣赏方案的Python代码简洁性，并提供了一个示例。
• [noman-land] 提到Cryptosteel作为类似产品，但未被其他人提及。
• [thih9] 担心长时间后会忘记解码方法，建议直接雕刻常规字符更简单。
• [Mraedis] 觉得方案愚蠢但有趣，个人更倾向于直接在石板上打印文字。
• [msk-lywenn] 认为这个方案像新的二维条码，质疑为何不直接使用有冗余的QR码。
• [deadbabe] 建议开发一个用户界面，以便更快输入1和0，而不是点击复选框。

• 争议焦点：方案的实用性与复杂性之间的平衡。部分人认为直接使用现有技术如QR码更简单，而其他人则欣赏方案的创意和手工操作的趣味。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：包括存储环境的考虑、信息密度和可读性的提升、以及不同加密方法的实现和安全性讨论。

data.title: A Lean companion to Analysis I
data.author: jeremyscanvic
data.article_summary: 作者大约20年前编写了《Analysis I》这本实分析教材，专注于基础问题，如自然数、整数、有理数和实数的构造，以及提供足够的集合论和逻辑知识以帮助学生进行严谨的证明。虽然编写时未考虑形式化验证，但随着对证明助手的了解，作者意识到该书内容与Lead等证明助手兼容。因此，作者推出了《Analysis I》的Lead配套项目，将书中的定义、定理和练习“翻译”成Lead代码，允许通过填补代码中的“sorries”来完成练习。该项目目前已翻译了部分章节，并有意在后续章节中更多依赖Lean的Mathlib库。作者欢迎志愿者测试该项目并提供反馈，以确保练习能在Lead中顺利完成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用Lean进行数学教学的优点、挑战以及相关资源和工具的比较

不同观点：
• **立即反馈的优势**：ubj认为Lean的编译器可以提供即时反馈，这比等待人工反馈更有效率，并建议未来可以提供更具指导性的反馈，类似于Rust编译器的建议功能。
• **学习曲线的挑战**：danabramov和brosco认为Lean和Mathlib的学习曲线较陡，尤其是Mathlib的复杂性可能对初学者造成困难，但同时他们也认为这是将数学书籍与工具连接起来的有益尝试。
• **工具选择的理由不明确**：thdhhghgbhy指出作者未详细解释为何选择Lean而非Coq或Agda。
• **数学教育的激进观点**：UltraSane主张数学教育应侧重于计算机代数系统和定理证明器的构建，强调实用性和可视化，而非传统的纸笔计算。
• **教材与形式化证明的对比**：jhanschoo担心Mathlib中使用的过滤器概念与传统教材中的epsilon-delta方法存在差异，可能会对教学造成困扰。
• **资源和项目的分享**：IssaRice列举了多个尝试将Tao的Analysis I形式化到Lean的项目和资源，指出了这些项目大多停留在前几章，并分享了相关的GitHub链接。

补充讨论：
• **Lean在不同数学领域的应用**：nextos提到定理证明在编程语言理论中已有应用，并认为分析中的定理相对更难，建议从 simpler starting point 开始。
• **Lean在主流教材与形式化数学库中的比较**：zozbot234讨论了主流教材与Mathlib在教授实分析时的不同方法，并提出了是否应在学术课程中教授Mathlib版本的问题。
• **具体领域的学习资源**：331c8c71询问使用Lean学习线性代数的起点，westurner则提到HoTT（同伦类型论）作为数学基础的替代方案，并分享了相关资源。
• ** isomorphism 的相关性**：practal质疑证明 isomorphism 到Mathlib等价的重要性，并询问是否可以省略这一部分。

争议焦点：
• **Mathlib的复杂性与教学适用性**：一部分讨论者认为Mathlib的复杂性和快速变化可能不适合作为教学工具，而另一部分讨论者则认为这是一种有益的挑战和学习机会。
• **工具选择的理由**：部分讨论者对选择Lean而非其他定理证明器表示疑惑，认为需要更明确的解释。

总结：讨论围绕使用Lean进行数学教学的优缺点展开，涉及学习资源的分享、工具选择的合理性以及具体教学方法的适用性等问题。

44145517.article_content:
Almost 20 years ago, I wrote a textbook in real analysis called “
Analysis I
“. It was intended to complement the many good available analysis textbooks out there by focusing more on foundational issues, such as the construction of the natural numbers, integers, rational numbers, and reals, as well as providing enough set theory and logic to allow students to develop proofs at high levels of rigor.
While some proof assistants such as Coq or Agda were well established when the book was written, formal verification was not on my radar at the time. However, now that I have had some experience with this subject, I realize that the content of this book is in fact very compatible with such proof assistants; in particular, the ‘naive type theory’ that I was implicitly using to do things like construct the standard number systems, dovetails well with the dependent type theory of Lean (which, among other things, has excellent support for quotient types).
I have therefore decided to launch a
Lean companion to “Analysis I”
, which is a “translation” of many of the definitions, theorems, and exercises of the text into Lean. In particular, this gives an alternate way to perform the exercises in the book, by instead filling in the corresponding “sorries” in the Lean code. (I do not however plan on hosting “official” solutions to the exercises in this companion; instead, feel free to create forks of the repository in which these sorries are filled in.)
Currently, the following sections of the text have been translated into Lean:
Section 2.1: The natural numbers
Section 2.2: Addition
Section 2.3: Multiplication
Chapter 2 epilogue: Isomorphism with the Mathlib natural numbers
Section 3.1: Basic set theory
Section 4.1: The integers
The formalization has been deliberately designed to be separate from the standard Lean math library
Mathlib
at some places, but reliant on it at others. For instance, Mathlib already has a standard notion of the natural numbers
. In the Lean formalization, I first develop “by hand” an alternate construction
Chapter2.Nat
of the natural numbers (or just
Nat
, if one is working in the
Chapter2
namespace), setting up many of the basic results about these alternate natural numbers which parallel similar lemmas about
that are already in Mathlib (but with many of these lemmas set as exercises to the reader, with the proofs currently replaced with “sorries”). Then, in an epilogue section, isomorphisms between these alternate natural numbers and the Mathlib natural numbers are established (or more precisely, set as exercises). From that point on, the Chapter 2 natural numbers are deprecated, and the Mathlib natural numbers are used instead. I intend to continue this general pattern throughout the book, so that as one advances into later chapters, one increasingly relies on Mathlib’s definitions and functions, rather than directly referring to any counterparts from earlier chapters. As such, this companion could also be used as an introduction to Lean and Mathlib as well as to real analysis (somewhat in the spirit of the “
Natural number game
“, which in fact has significant thematic overlap with Chapter 2 of my text).
(One technical note: for my own convenience, I have placed this companion as a subdirectory of another one of my repositories, which was aimed at formalizing the theory of orders of magnitude discussed in
this previous blog post
. I may eventually split off this companion into its own repository, but at this stage I think it is workable to host two largely independent projects in the same repository.)
The code in this repository compiles in Lean, but I have not tested whether all of the (numerous) “sorries” in the code can actually be filled (i.e., if all the exercises can actually be solved in Lean). I would be interested in having volunteers “playtest” the companion to see if this can actually be done (and if the helper lemmas or “API” provided in the Lean files are sufficient to fill in the sorries in a conceptually straightforward manner without having to rely on more esoteric Lean programming techniques). Any other feedback will of course also be welcome.

data.title: Oxfordshire clock still keeping village on time after 500 years
data.article_summary: 东亨德雷德村的圣奥古斯丁教堂钟楼时钟已运行500年，被认为是英国最古老的仍在原址运行的时钟之一。该时钟没有钟面，通过教堂钟声每刻报时，并通过一个类似巨大音乐盒的装置每天四次播放曲子。2015年，时钟因故障停摆，经过修复和安装自动上弦系统后恢复运行。本周，村民们庆祝了时钟500周年，并有机会参观其运行机制。尽管受天气影响，时钟的精准度在历史上相当出色。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：历史悠久的村庄教堂钟声及其时间keeping功能

不同观点：
• [alfanick] 认为村庄教堂的钟声虽然起初可能令人烦恼，但最终会习惯并利用其判断时间。他描述了钟声的不同模式，包括每小时一次以及每15分钟一次的钟声，并且早上6点会有长达5分钟的钟声音乐，像是在提醒人们起床工作。

• [rajnathani] 提到这种基于重力机制的钟需要定期手动上发条，因此不可能连续运行500年。他通过提到"verge escapements"机制，对钟的运作原理进行了技术补充。

• [Daub] 指出，在铁路出现之前，不同村庄根据教堂钟的时间定义各自的“时区”，而铁路的普及结束了这种现象。这提供了一个历史背景，说明钟声在过去如何影响人们的时间观念。

• [pm215] 提供了2014年的钟运作视频链接，展示了钟在修复之前的情况，为讨论增加了视觉资料。

• [julian55] 分享了他们的村庄也有类似的无面钟，并提供了一个链接，指向村庄教堂钟的网页，提供了实际例子。

• [Archelaos] 提到萨利斯堡大教堂的一个1386年的钟，提供了另一个历史悠久钟的例子，丰富了讨论的历史维度。

• [layer8] 提到附近建筑上的日晷依然保持时间，增加了关于古老时间keeping设备的更多例子。

• [mattgrice] 以幽默方式回应了关于钟准确性的讨论，表示对钟的准确性感到满意。

• [mike-the-mikado] 提供了有关该村庄行政区划变动的历史信息，指出该地在1974年之前属于伯克郡，增加了讨论的地理和历史背景。

• [cnewey] 以个人经历回应，提到自己住在讨论中的村庄，并能从卧室窗户看到教堂，为讨论增加了个人和地方色彩。

• [eleveriven] 强调钟声与日常生活和社区紧密联系的历史，认为这是一种温馨的提醒。

• [smitty1e] 以幽默方式讨论了钟的现代化升级，提到机械化上发条系统的安装，结束了手动上发条的需求。

• [madaxe_again] 提出关于设备历史完整性的讨论，认为钟的某些部分可能经过了多次修复和更换，引发了关于设备真实历史年代的争议。

• 争议焦点在于钟的历史完整性，特别是在[madaxe_again]提出的修复和现代化的讨论中，不同部件的年代和修复历史引发了关于钟是否仍然保持其原始状态的讨论。
• 讨论中多次提到钟的准确性和运作原理，以及其在社区中的功能和重要性，反映了人们对历史悠久的公共设施的关注和欣赏。
• 个人经历和地方背景的分享增加了讨论的生动性和多样性，如[cnewey]的个人见闻和[mike-the-mikado]的历史地理信息。

44122860.article_content:
Clock still keeping village on time after 500 years
4 days ago
Share
Save
Joe Campbell
BBC News
Share
Save
BBC
St Augustine's clock in East Hendred has been keeping time since Henry VIII was on the throne.
Villagers have been celebrating the 500th birthday of the clock in their parish church.
The timepiece in East Hendred, near Wantage in rural Oxfordshire, is believed to be one of the oldest clocks in Britain still in its original location.
With no clock face or hands, it relies on the church bells in the tower at St Augustine's to ring out the time every quarter hour.
The decision to install it in the church was taken when Henry VIII was on the throne, explained the man responsible for St Augustine's bells, Tower Captain Nigel Findley.
"Imagine the excitement that would have caused then," he said.
The clock is linked to a carillon which uses winches and pulleys to drive hammers high above that strike the bells every quarter hour.
As well as striking the bells every quarter hour, a carillon resembling the insides of a giant musical box, plays a tune called Angel's Song four times a day, every three hours, starting at 09:00.
In 2015, one of the hammers used to strike the six bells came away and fell into the mechanism, jamming it and silencing the clock.
"It was like missing a friend," said church council secretary Ann Pappenheim. "It's a real part of living in the village.
"When you're working in the garden, it really does give you a sense of time and I missed it," she added. "Now it's back and it's wonderful."
The clock, which was originally built a few miles away in Wantage, underwent a lengthy renovation.
A modification also saw the installation of a mechanised winding system, ending the requirement for somebody to climb the narrow, winding staircase each day to the clock room to do the job by hand.
With no clock face on the tower the timepiece relies on the church bells to signal the time
This week, to mark the clock's birthday, people were able to visit the tower to see the mechanism in action.
Acting as guide was Simon Gilchrist, who led the restoration.
He described it as being "a real passion," to have spent time on the project.
"It's not often that we as clock repairers get the opportunity to work on something that is old, but also something that is of great historical importance," he said.
The clock used to be set using a sundial on the outside of the tower. Now a modern digital clock secured to the wall, next to the Tudor era mechanism is used.
"When this thing was made 500 years ago, we didn't have the accuracy that we have today," said Mr Gilchrist.
Parts of the mechanism like the pendulum expand in the summers heat and contract in the cold of winter, all affecting timekeeping.
This was a device built for a time when peoples' days began at dawn and ended shortly after the sun went down.
Given that, he added: "In terms if accuracy, it's pretty accurate."

• [alfanick] 认为村庄教堂的钟声虽然起初可能令人烦恼，但最终会习惯并利用其判断时间。他描述了钟声的不同模式，包括每小时一次以及每15分钟一次的钟声，并且早上6点会有长达5分钟的钟声音乐，像是在提醒人们起床工作。

• [rajnathani] 提到这种基于重力机制的钟需要定期手动上发条，因此不可能连续运行500年。他通过提到"verge escapements"机制，对钟的运作原理进行了技术补充。

• [Daub] 指出，在铁路出现之前，不同村庄根据教堂钟的时间定义各自的“时区”，而铁路的普及结束了这种现象。这提供了一个历史背景，说明钟声在过去如何影响人们的时间观念。

• [pm215] 提供了2014年的钟运作视频链接，展示了钟在修复之前的情况，为讨论增加了视觉资料。

• [Archelaos] 提到萨利斯堡大教堂的一个1386年的钟，提供了另一个历史悠久钟的例子，丰富了讨论的历史维度。

• [layer8] 提到附近建筑上的日晷依然保持时间，增加了关于古老时间keeping设备的更多例子。

• [mattgrice] 以幽默方式回应了关于钟准确性的讨论，表示对钟的准确性感到满意。

• [mike-the-mikado] 提供了有关该村庄行政区划变动的历史信息，指出该地在1974年之前属于伯克郡，增加了讨论的地理和历史背景。

data.title: Sguaba: Hard-to-misuse rigid body transforms for engineers
data.author: lukastyrychtr
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个名为Sguaba的Rust库，旨在简化处理不同坐标系之间转换的过程，特别是针对工程师而非数学专家。Sguaba通过强类型系统避免不同坐标系间的混淆，支持如WGS84、ECEF、NED、FRD等坐标系，并提供这些系统之间的转换功能。它利用Rust的类型系统防止错误使用，并附有详细文档解释理论和实践。文章通过一个飞行员观察物体位置的示例，展示了如何使用Sguaba在不同坐标系间进行转换，强调了安全构造转换的重要性。Sguaba的目标是让工程师专注于其他重要任务，而不必深究线性代数细节。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：强类型坐标变换在生产环境中的应用及其优势与挑战

不同观点：
• [fsloth] 支持强类型坐标系统，认为通过强类型来区分不同坐标系可以有效避免许多潜在的错误。他建议为不同坐标系创建特定类型，并实现所需的代数运算，从而提高代码的健壮性。
• [techbro92] 表示曾遇到由于向量在错误坐标系中表达而导致的细微错误，认为类似强类型方案值得考虑。
• [kaibee] 通过在游戏开发中的实际经验证实了强类型向量的优势，并提到使用AI生成C#代码，实现了类型安全的Vector3，从而节省了大量时间。
• [avs733] 认为这种强类型方案在航空航天等行业推广时会遇到验证问题，因为这些行业更关注系统的稳定性和历史遗留代码（如MATLAB和Fortran）。他还提出可变精度类型的选项可能是一个有趣的补充。
• [Animats] 对新增Rust向量和矩阵库持怀疑态度，认为过多的类似库会导致几何处理中的麻烦。他更关注语言设计的早期决策对后续开发的影响，并指出Rust在基本类型和错误处理方面的一些问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了具体实现的例子和代码片段（如kaibee提供的C#代码链接），展示了强类型坐标系统的实际应用。
• 针对航空航天行业的讨论，指出历史遗留系统和技术惯性对新技术推广的阻碍，强调了稳定性和兼容性的重要性。
• 关于Rust语言设计的问题，提出了对基本数据类型和错误处理的关注，反映出语言设计早期决策对后续开发的影响。

争议焦点：
• 强类型坐标系统在不同行业中的实际应用价值和推广难度。
• 新增Rust库的必要性及其对几何处理的影响。
• Rust语言设计中基本类型的合理性和早期决策的长期影响。

data.title: New adaptive optics shows details of our star's atmosphere
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 科学家开发了一种新的“日冕自适应光学系统”，首次拍摄到太阳日冕层的最清晰图像和视频。该系统安装在美国新泽西理工学院运营的1.6米Goode太阳望远镜上，能够消除地球大气湍流造成的图像模糊。这些高分辨率图像展示了日冕中精细结构的快速变化，包括日珥的重组和等离子体流的形成与崩溃，还首次清晰捕捉到“日冕雨”现象，即冷却的等离子体凝结后落回太阳表面。这些观测为研究日冕加热、太阳爆发和空间天气提供了新的视角，并可能带来更多科学发现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太阳观测技术及其相关科学现象的讨论

不同观点：
• Adam认为，文章中最有趣的创新并不是可变形镜面，而是聚焦于日冕特征的波前传感器设计，这与之前的系统聚焦于太阳表面的“颗粒”不同。
• Itishappy感叹观测的视野规模之大，表现出对天文尺度的惊叹。
• Krunck被第一视频中的稳定结构所吸引，指出虽然整体结构保持不变，但其内部却充满动态变化。
• So-rose表达了对观测太阳表面现象（如太阳针状体）的兴奋，并提到这些现象的物理机制仍在激烈争论中。
• Srean提到自适应光学技术起源于SDI资助的秘密空间武器研究，并指出这一技术曾在不同领域被独立提出。
• Tomrod简单表达了对视频美丽程度的赞赏。
• Whatshisface呼吁观众通过联系国会议员来支持此类研究。
• Ambicapter提出是否可以通过在人造卫星上设置可重新定位的光源来校准和获取更精确的大气畸变数据。
• Jeremyscanvic对其同事在理论天文成像研究中的工作表示赞赏，并认为这种下游应用非常有趣。
• Kadushka质疑“最清晰的图像”为何不是来自更接近太阳的空间拍摄。
• Casenmgreen的评论与其他讨论无关，提到阻止Tor用户。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及的科学机制包括太阳针状体的物理机制，这一机制仍是科学界争论的焦点。
- 技术的历史背景也被提及，特别是自适应光学技术与秘密武器研究的历史渊源。
- 有对天文观测规模的感叹，以及对未来可能的技术改进（如人造星或卫星光源）的设想。
- 不同观众对同一视频内容的关注点各异，从技术细节到政策呼吁，再到纯粹的美学欣赏。

44147573.article_content:
“Raindrops in the Sun’s Corona”: New Adaptive Optics Shows Stunning Details of our Star’s Atmosphere
Credit: Schmidt et al./NJIT/NSO/AURA/NSF
Home
»
“Raindrops in the Sun’s Corona”: New Adaptive Optics Shows Stunning Details of our Star’s Atmosphere
Release Date:
May 27, 2025
Scientists from the U.S. National Science Foundation National Solar Observatory and New Jersey Institute of Technology produced the finest images of the Sun’s corona to date. To make these high-resolution images and movies, the team developed a new ‘coronal adaptive optics’ system that removes blur from images caused by the Earth’s atmosphere. Their ground-breaking results were recently published in Nature Astronomy and pave the way for deeper insight into coronal heating, solar eruptions, and space weather, and open an opportunity for new discoveries in the Sun’s atmosphere.
Scientists develop new optical system that removes blur over fine-structure in the Sun’s corona, revealing clearest images to date
BOULDER, CO, Tuesday, May 27, 2025
–
The Sun’s corona—the outermost layer of its atmosphere, visible only during a total solar eclipse—has long intrigued scientists due to its extreme temperatures, violent eruptions, and large prominences. However, turbulence in the Earth’s atmosphere has caused image blur and hindered observations of the corona. A ground-breaking recent development by scientists from the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) National Solar Observatory (NSO), and New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT), is changing that by using adaptive optics to remove the blur.
As published in
Nature Astronomy
, this pioneering ‘coronal adaptive optics’ technology has produced the most astonishing, clearest images and videos of fine-structure in the corona to date. This development will open the door for deeper insights into the corona’s enigmatic behavior and the processes driving space weather.
Most Detailed Coronal Images to Date Revealed
Funded by the NSF and installed at the 1.6-meter Goode Solar Telescope (GST), operated by NJIT’s Center for Solar-Terrestrial Research (CSTR) at Big Bear Solar Observatory (BBSO) in California, “Cona”—the adaptive optics system responsible for these new images—compensates for the blur caused by air turbulence in the Earth’s atmosphere —similar to the bumpy air passengers feel during a flight.
“The turbulence in the air severely degrades images of objects in space, like our Sun, seen through our telescopes. But we can correct for that,”
says Dirk Schmidt, NSO Adaptive Optics Scientist who led the development.
Among the team’s remarkable observations is a movie of a quickly restructuring solar prominence unveiling fine, turbulent internal flows. Solar prominences are large, bright features, often appearing as arches or loops, extending outward from the Sun’s surface.
https://nso.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Prominence-1-Video.mp4
This image of a prominence above the solar surface is a snapshot of a 4-minute time-lapse movie that reveals its rapid, fine, and turbulent restructuring with unprecedented detail. The Sun’s fluffy-looking surface is covered by “spicules”, short-lived plasma jets, whose creation is still the subject of scientific debate. The streaks on the right of this image are coronal rain falling down onto the Sun’s surface. This image was taken by the Goode Solar Telescope at Big Bear Solar Observatory using the new coronal adaptive optics system Cona. The image shows the hydrogen-alpha light emitted by the solar plasma. The image is artificially colorized, yet based on the color of hydrogen-alpha light, and darker color is brighter light. Credit: Schmidt et al./NJIT/NSO/AURA/NSF
A second movie replays the rapid formation and collapse of a finely structured plasma stream.
“These are by far the most detailed observations of this kind, showing features not previously observed, and it’s not quite clear what they are,”
says Vasyl Yurchyshyn, co-author of the study and NJIT-CSTR research professor. “
It is super exciting to build an instrument that shows us the Sun like never before,
” Schmidt adds.
https://nso.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Plasmoid-Video.mp4
This image was taken by the Goode Solar Telescope at Big Bear Solar Observatory using the new coronal adaptive optics system Cona. The image shows the hydrogen-alpha light emitted by the solar plasma. The image is artificially colorized, yet based on the color of hydrogen-alpha light, and darker color is brighter light.
Credit:
Schmidt et al./NJIT/NSO/AURA/NSF
A third movie shows fine strands of coronal rain—a phenomenon where cooling plasma condenses and falls back toward the Sun’s surface. “
Raindrops in the Sun’s corona can be narrower than 20 kilometers,”
NSO Astronomer Thomas Schad concludes from the most detailed images of coronal rain to date, “
These findings offer new invaluable observational insight that is vital to test computer models of coronal processes.
”
https://nso.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Coronal-Rain-Vi

data.title: Show HN: Open-source P2P file transfer
data.author: goodpanda
data.article_summary: Berb是一个简化的P2P文件共享平台，采用隐私优先的设计。它利用WebRTC技术，无需服务器或上传文件，直接在设备间传输文件，确保安全和快速。主要特点包括通过WebRTC数据通道直接连接用户，文件不经过服务器。当前开发任务包括网络断开自动重连、多文件支持以及在支持的浏览器上保存流。贡献代码前需先开启一个讨论。技术栈包括Node.js、JavaScript、WebRTC、P2P和Pug。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Iroh's Sendme 项目的技术细节、安全性及其替代方案

不同观点：
• [satvikpendem] 提出了对 Iroh's Sendme 项目的关注，并分享了项目链接，表明对该项目的兴趣。
• [howtofly] 认为信令服务器可能成为中间人攻击的理想位置，并指出项目的README文件未提及如何解决这一安全问题。
• [ranger_danger] 提到尽管项目声称"无服务器"，但由于对称NAT或CGNAT的广泛存在，许多用户仍需要TURN服务器来实现P2P连接，并表示自己从未成功使用类似p2p/WebRTC的网站。
• [fabrice_d] 关心ICE协议的offer/answer交换过程是否通过用户服务器上的WebSocket实现，询问该项目的具体技术实现方式。
• [pwn0] 对项目的开源许可和贡献指南提出建议，希望项目添加相关信息以方便他人参与。
• [opengears] 提到该项目的替代方案，推荐了LocalSend作为另一个类似工具。
• [evbogue] 探讨了浏览器直接连接的技术挑战，特别是NAT穿透的问题，并分享了一个相关工具（Trystero），认为该领域需要更多研究。

data.title: RenderFormer: Neural rendering of triangle meshes with global illumination
data.author: klavinski
data.article_summary: RenderFormer是一种基于Transformer的神经渲染管道，能够直接从场景的三角形表示渲染图像，支持全局光照效果，且无需针对每个场景进行训练或微调。它采用端到端的序列转换方法，将具有反射属性的三角形序列转换为小图像块序列。该方法分为两个阶段：视图无关阶段处理三角形间光传输，视图相关阶段将光束转换为像素值。整个过程不依赖光栅化或光线追踪，并展示了在不同光照、材质和几何复杂度下的渲染效果，以及动态场景和物理模拟的渲染能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于RenderFormer等神经渲染技术在速度、质量、应用场景和局限性等方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持神经渲染的效率和潜力**：
  - **timhigins**: 强调RenderFormer在速度上的巨大优势，尤其是在3D设计预览中的潜在应用。尽管目前在复杂场景中不够准确，但速度提升可能足以让大型动画工作室在预览阶段使用。
  - **vessenes**: 认为这是一个非常酷的研究，transformer架构的多功能性令人印象深刻。对实际场景的演示充满期待。
  - **nicklo**: 提到这是图形渲染中的“惨痛教训”，即通过数据和注意力来实现渲染，而非依赖传统的先验知识和方法。

• **质疑神经渲染的应用和必要性**：
  - **dclowd9901**: 质疑这种方法在实际应用中是否比直接方法更快，并询问其使用场景。
  - **kookamamie**: 认为渲染结果有些模糊，期望看到与传统渲染器的比较。

• **讨论神经渲染在游戏和图形领域的具体应用**：
  - **hualaka**: 询问神经渲染在游戏渲染中的效率。
  - **mixedbit**: 提到深度学习在去噪方面的成功应用，传统光线追踪算法结合神经网络可以提高效率。

• **指出神经渲染的局限性和不足**：
  - **notnullorvoid**: 指出渲染示例中没有展示摄像机后面的内容，这在反射和照明计算中是重要的，可能是一个局限。
  - **CyberDildonics**: 强调论文中没有展示多边形、纹理、运动模糊、景深等细节，认为现代GPU在制作类似30年前计算效果的图像，有一定的局限性。

补充讨论：
• **关于行业应用和人才需求**：
  - **coalteddy**: 提到电影行业中对基于物理的渲染器的需求，并表示有朋友正在寻找相关机会，询问AI公司是否也在招聘渲染工程师。

• **关于技术实现和架构的讨论**：
  - **jmpeax**: 询问交叉注意力和自我注意力的优先级问题。
  - **goatmanbah**: 感叹transformer的广泛应用，似乎没有什么是不能做的。

• **关于技术哲学的反思**：
  - **keyle**: 将神经渲染比喻为“黑客帝国版光线追踪”，感觉像是一个奇特的轮回。

争议的焦点：
• 神经渲染在复杂场景中的准确性和最终渲染的质量是否足以替代传统方法。
• 神经渲染在实际应用中的效率和必要性，特别是在游戏渲染和电影制作中的具体表现。

44148524.article_content:
Introduction
We present RenderFormer, a neural rendering pipeline that directly renders an image from a triangle-based representation of a scene with full global illumination effects and that
does not require per-scene training or fine-tuning
.
Mesh to Image, End to End
Instead of taking a physics-centric approach to rendering, we formulate rendering as a
sequence-to-sequence transformation
where a sequence of tokens representing triangles with reflectance properties is converted to a sequence of output tokens representing small patches of pixels.
Simple Transformer Architecture with Minimal Prior Constraints
RenderFormer follows a two stage pipeline: a view-independent stage that models triangle-to-triangle light transport, and a view-dependent stage that transforms a token representing a bundle of rays to the corresponding pixel values guided by the triangle-sequence from the the view-independent stage. Both stages are based on the transformer architecture and are learned with minimal prior constraints.
No rasterization, no ray tracing.
Rendering Gallery
Examples of scenes rendered with RenderFormer demonstrating various lighting conditions, materials, and geometric complexity, without any per-scene training or fine-tuning. Check out the
reference images
for more details.

data.title: Ovld – Efficient and featureful multiple dispatch for Python
data.author: breuleux
data.article_summary: `ovld` 是一个用于 Python 的高级多重调度库，允许根据函数参数的类型和值进行调度，而无需使用 `isinstance` 语句。它支持多参数调度，速度快，并提供多种高级功能，如变体、混合和依赖类型。通过装饰器定义不同版本的函数来处理不同类型和值，还支持递归定义和代码生成。此外，`ovld` 允许设置优先级和使用 `call_next` 来控制调度顺序，适用于调试和扩展。示例展示了如何处理基本类型、列表和依赖类型的函数定义与调用，如阶乘计算。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于API设计、多重派发（multimethods）的实用性及其实现效率的讨论

不同观点：
• **对API设计的肯定与质疑**：
   - **支持观点**：linschn认为该API设计很符合Python风格，且合理。
   - **质疑观点**：linschn同时提到"Greenspun's tenth rule"，暗示可能有更简洁的解决方案（如Lisp），虽然该实现并非有bug，但引发了其对是否过度复杂的思考。

• **多重派发的实际应用场景**：
   - **困惑与需求**：paddy_m表示对多重派发、多方法和CLOS方法特化感到混淆，并请求实际使用场景的例子，以更好地理解何时使用多重派发。
   - **实际应用反馈**：paddy_m希望了解其他人是否在实际问题中使用过多重派发，效果如何，是否会再次使用。

• **实现效率的探讨**：
   - **对性能的关注**：ziihrs对该实现为何比其他替代方案更快表示好奇，并建议使用PyPy进行基准测试以验证性能。

• **对复杂代码库的担忧**：
   - **批评观点**：photios对继承复杂、重载过多的代码库表示担忧，认为这会给后续开发者带来麻烦。

• **与类型提示的兼容性**：
   - **技术问题**：olejorgenb关注该实现是否与类型提示（typehints）兼容，质疑装饰器能否输出@overload。

• **对命名方式的调侃**：
   - **轻松评论**：blu3h4t开玩笑地提到该命名像是某个著名Perl黑客的昵称。

• **对同步与异步派发的需求**：
   - **功能扩展建议**：est提出是否可以同时支持同步和异步派发，并分享了一个相关链接（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43982570）。

• **对主流语言直接支持多重派发的疑问**：
   - **质疑主流语言的设计**：rahulprasath质疑为何像Python这样的主流语言不直接支持多重派发。

补充讨论：
- 多重派发在实际项目中的应用场景及其实际效果是讨论的一个核心，paddy_m和ziihrs都提到了对该功能实用性的关注。
- 对API设计复杂度的思考和代码库可维护性的担忧也是讨论的重点，部分评论者如photios和linschn对此表达了保留意见。
- 技术细节如类型提示的兼容性和性能优化（ziihrs提到的PyPy测试）也是重要的讨论内容。
- 一些评论如blu3h4t的调侃和est的功能建议则提供了较为轻松或建设性的视角。

Ovld
Fast multiple dispatch in Python, with many extra features.
📋 Documentation
With ovld, you can write a version of the same function for every type signature using annotations instead of writing an awkward sequence of
isinstance
statements. Unlike Python's
singledispatch
, it works for multiple arguments.
⚡️
Fast
:
ovld is the fastest multiple dispatch library around, by some margin.
🚀
Variants
,
mixins
and
medleys
of functions and methods.
🦄
Dependent types
:
Overloaded functions can depend on more than argument types: they can depend on actual values.
🔑
Extensive
:
Dispatch on functions, methods, positional arguments and even keyword arguments (with some restrictions).
⚙️
Codegen
:
(Experimental) For advanced use cases, you can generate custom code for overloads.

pip install ovld

data.author: lowdanie
data.article_summary:
本文主要讨论了量子算法中著名的隐藏子群问题（Hidden Subgroup Problem, HSP），尤其是交换群情况下的解决方法，并介绍了Shor算法和Simon问题的量子解决方案。

隐藏子群问题旨在通过给定的黑盒函数$f$，找出隐藏的子群$H$。对于交换群，存在一种称为“标准方法”的量子算法，能够高效解决HSP，其复杂度为$\mathcal{O}(\log(|G|))$，优于经典算法的$\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{|G|})$。

Shor算法可用于整数分解和离散对数问题，这些都属于HSP的特例。Simon问题则是一个展示经典计算困难而量子计算高效的典型例子：给定一个函数$f$，需要找出满足特定条件的秘密比特串$\mathbf{s}$。量子算法通过少量查询即可确定该比特串，而经典算法通常需要更多的计算。

本文还详细描述了量子傅里叶变换（QFT）在解决这些问题中的应用。

Introduction
Two of the most famous
quantum algorithms
are
Shor’s Algorithms
for
integer factorization
and
discrete logarithms
.
The significance of these algorithms is that efficient integer factorization breaks
the
RSA cryptosystem
,
and efficient discrete logarithm computation
breaks the
Diffie-Hellman
key exchange protocol.
It is natural to wonder what other types of problems that are classically considered
to be hard can be efficiently solved with a quantum computer.
Interestingly, both integer factorization and the discrete logarithm problem
are special cases of a more general problem called the
hidden subgroup problem
(HSP).
Furthermore, Shor’s algorithms can be generalized to an efficient quantum
algorithm for the HSP whenever the group in question is
commutative
.
Conversely,
almost all
known problems with significant quantum speedups are
instances of the HSP for commutative groups.
In this post we’ll introduce the hidden subgroup problem and the quantum
algorithm that efficiently solves it in the commutative case. We’ll also apply this
framework to the discrete logarithm problem and
Simon’s Problem
.
The Hidden Subgroup Problem
In this section we’ll formally define the hidden subgroup problem and then see
how it generalizes some famous problems in quantum computing.
We’ll start by defining the notion of a function on a group
hiding
a subgroup.
Definition (Hiding A Subgroup).
Let $G$ be a finite group, $H\subset G$ a
subgroup of $G$, $A$ a set and
\[f: G \rightarrow A\]
a function from $G$ to $A$.
We say that $f$
hides
$H$ if, for all $g_1,g_2\in G$,
$f(g_1) = f(g_2)$ if and only if $g_1H = g_2H$.
In other words, $f$ hides $H$ if it defines an injective function on the cosets of $H$.
The
hidden subgroup problem
is to find $H$ given an black box which allows
us to evaluate $f$ on elements of $G$.
Definition (Hidden Subgroup Problem).
Let $G$ be a finite group, $H\subset G$
a subgroup and
$f: G \rightarrow A$ a function that hides $H$.
The objective of the
hidden subgroup problem
(HSP) is to find generators for
$H$ using evaluations of a black box for $f$.
It’s always possible to solve an instance of the hidden subgroup problem
with $\mathcal{O}(|G|)$ evaluations of $f$. Indeed, we can evaluate $f$ on every element of
$G$ and note that:
\[H = \{g\in G | f(g) = f(e) \}\]
where $e\in G$ denotes the identity element in $G$.
The interesting question is whether we can find generators for $H$ more efficiently.
When $G$ is
abelian
, there is a generalization
of
Shor’s algorithm
called
the standard method
which
solves the HSP with only $\mathcal{O}(\log(|G|)$ invocations of
$f$. In contrast, there are many interesting instances of the ableian HSP where the best known
classical algorithm requires $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{|G|})$ invocations.
Below we’ll consider two important instances of the abelian HSG. We’ll then describe
the standard method and apply it to each example.
Simon’s Problem
Simon’s problem was introduced by
Daniel Simon
in 1994 as
an example of a problem which classically requires nearly exponential time, but can be
efficiently solved with a quantum computer.
Let $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^N$ be the group of bit-strings of length $N$ and let
$\oplus$ denote the bitwise XOR operation.
For example, if $N=3$ then $110$ and $101$ are elements of $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^3$ and:
\[110 \oplus 101 = 011\]
Simon’s problem is defined as follow:
We are given access to a black-box for computing a function
\[f: (\mathbb{Z}/2)^N \rightarrow A\]
from $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^N$ to a set $A$. In addition, we are promised
that there is a secret bit-string $\mathbf{s}\in (\mathbb{Z}/2)^N$ such that for all
$\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}’\in(\mathbb{Z}/2)^N$,
$f(\mathbf{x}) = f(\mathbf{x}’)$ if and only if $\mathbf{x}’ = \mathbf{x}$ or
$\mathbf{x}’ = \mathbf{x} \oplus \mathbf{s}$. The challenge is to find $\mathbf{s}$
with as few calls as possible to the black box for $f$.
To get some intuition for the role of the secret bit-string $\mathbf{s}$,
consider the following function on $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^3$ where $A = (\mathbb{Z}/2)^2$:
$\mathbf{x}$
$f(\mathbf{x})$
$000$
$10$
$001$
$00$
$010$
$11$
$011$
$01$
$100$
$00$
$101$
$10$
$110$
$01$
$111$
$11$
It is easy to check that in this case the solution to Simon’s problem is
$\mathbf{s}=101$. Note that $f$ is a 2 to 1 function. In general, we can think
of $\mathbf{s}$ as a bitmask where $f(\mathbf{x}) = f(\mathbf{x}’)$ if and only
if $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{x}’$ differ exactly at the elements masked by
$\mathbf{s}$.

44148853.article_content:
Kilnettle Shrine Talking Tape Dispenser - Stephen Coyle
Stephen Coyle
home
about
6 July, 2024
Kilnettle Shrine Talking Tape Dispenser
A couple of years ago I wrote
this
post, wherein I detail how I built a working version of the tape dispenser from Father Ted (
the one that says
you have used two inches of sticky tape, god bless you
). While it worked surprisingly well, that version had a number of flaws. It used unnecessarily overpowered hardware, was fragile, and didn’t sound very good.
Since making that one, I’d toyed with the idea of creating a better, more repeatable design. So, in very procrastinate-y fits and starts over the last few months, I’ve been doing just that.
This new one is much smaller, sounds better, and I daresay looks a touch more
professional
than its predecessor. Read on to find out how to get one of your own!
More importantly, it’s also much easier to make and I’ve got actual documentation for doing so. The case is 3D-printable, and all the parts print with no supports. Instead of a rotary encoder to measure the tape rotation, it now uses an IR led and sensor. The logic runs on an ESP8266 microcontroller instead of a Raspberry Pi Zero, all of which means the electronics inside can be purchased for less than €10.
It was a lot of fun improving on my 3D modelling, electronics, design and general planning skills in the process of making it. The initial body design was more complex, as was the circuitry, and I enjoyed iterating on and simplifying those significantly by the final product.
I did nurture the idea of actually selling these, but ultimately I think I’ve decided against it for now, for a few reasons:
Making one is fun, and a nice evening or weekend project. Making lots is more effort than I have time for at the moment.
I’ve got several earmarked for people already, and when I subtract those from the dozen I’ve made, I’m left with only a tiny batch to sell.
Factoring in the cost of components, time to assemble, and shipping, I don’t think there’s a compelling price point that doesn’t run at a loss. In which case I’d rather just give them away on my own terms.
How can you get one?
The good news, though, is that you can build one yourself! I’ve made the software, 3D-printable models, and instructions public on
GitHub
. You can also view the print files on
Printables
. It’s not a super complex build, so if you can manage basic soldering and have a 3D printer it’s probably a one-day project. I could potentially make kits, which contain all the required parts, that folks could assemble by themselves. If that's something you'd be interested in, do let me know. And if you do make one, or make some kind of remix, please send me pics!
Finally, and perhaps most importantly, if you do make one for yourself I'd appreciate if you made a donation to a charity that supports trans people. It's an awful shame that the creator of Father Ted is doing so much damage to an already vulnerable group, so anything that can help offset that is appreciated.

Description
Web browser extension (Firefox, Vivaldi, Chrome, Opera, Edge) to redirect URLs based on regex or wildcard patterns.
Tribute
In loving memory of Einar Egilsson, who gave us Redirector and selflessly nurtured it for many years.  We miss you Einar, and will always remember your kindness and generosity.
Download Links
Firefox
Google Chrome and Vivaldi
Examples
De-mobilizer
Example URL:
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/
Include pattern:
^(https?://)([a-z0-9-]*\.)m(?:obile)?\.(.*)
Redirect to:
$1$2$3
Pattern type: Regular Expression
Description: Always show the desktop version of websites
AMP redirect
Example URL:
https://www.google.com/amp/www.example.com/amp/document
Include pattern:
^(?:https?://)www.(?:google|bing).com/amp/(?:s/)?(.*)
Redirect to:
https://$1
Pattern type: Regular Expression
Description: AMP is bad:
https://80x24.net/post/the-problem-with-amp/
Doubleclick escaper
Example URL:
https://ad.doubleclick.net/ddm/trackclk/N135005.2681608PRIVATENETWORK/B20244?https://www.example.com
Include pattern:
^(?:https?://)ad.doubleclick.net/.*\?(http?s://.*)
Redirect to:
$1
Pattern type: Regular Expression
Description: Remove doubleclick link tracking / fix problems with doubleclick host-based blocking
YouTube Shorts to YouTube
Example URL:
https://www.youtube.com/shorts/video-id
Include pattern:
^(?:https?://)(?:www.)?youtube.com/shorts/([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)(.*)
Redirect to:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=$1$2
Pattern type: Regular Expression
Description: Redirect YouTube Shorts to regular YouTube
Fun with !bangs
What are bangs?:
https://duckduckgo.com/bangs
Use DuckDuckGo.com !bangs on Google
Example URL:
https://www.google.com/search?&ei=-FvkXcOVMo6RRwW5p5DgBg&q=asdfasdf%21+sadfas&oq=%21asdfasdf+sadfas&gs_l=asdfsadfafsgaf
Include pattern:
^(?:https?://)(?:www.)google\.(?:com|au|de|co\.uk)/search\?(?:.*)?(?:oq|q)=([^\&]*\+)?((?:%21|!)[^\&]*)
Redirect to:
https://duckduckgo.com/?q=$1$2
Pattern type: Regular Expression
Description: Redirect any Google query with a !bang to DDG
Custom DuckDuckGo.com !bangs
DDG !example Base
Example URL:
https://duckduckgo.com/?q=!
example
&get=other
Include pattern:
^(?:https?://)(?:.*\.)?duckduckgo.com/\?q=(?:%21|!)
example
(?=[^\+]|$)(?=\W|$)
Redirect to:

+searchterm2&get=other

example
)(?:\+([^\&\?\#]*))?(?:\W|$)

data.title: Structured Errors in Go (2022)
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了Go语言中错误管理的问题，特别是在中型程序和HTTP API中的应用。作者通过一系列实验，提出了一种简化错误处理的方法，并开发了一个新的库来实现这一目标。Go的错误处理通常依赖于返回值，而非异常机制，最简单的错误形式是字符串。虽然这种设计简单，但缺乏结构化信息。

文章强调了结构化日志的重要性，指出在错误管理中，错误信息需要被结构化，以便于日志聚合器和报警系统处理。传统上，错误信息是简单的字符串，难以进行有效的过滤和分析。为了改善这一情况，作者建议将错误信息结构化，例如在日志中加入"account_id"等具体字段，以便更好地诊断问题。

最终，作者提出了一种方法来弥合错误值和结构化日志之间的差距，并通过一个新库来实现这一功能，以提高错误管理的效率和可维护性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go 语言中错误处理和元数据管理的实现方式及其优缺点

不同观点：
• atombender 认为 `WithMeta()` 的实现有缺陷，既不支持并发安全，又会修改父 map。他建议使用树状结构来管理元数据，通过父节点指向之前的元数据，避免每次都分配新的 map。同时，他提出另一种方案，主张通过返回包含已知失败操作数据的结构化错误，并在错误上行过程中逐步添加元数据，这样只需在错误发生时付出性能代价。

• RadiozRadioz 强调错误不应该仅仅作为字符串返回，而应使用类或类型来区分不同种类的错误（如 HTTP 状态码 502 和 404），否则需要通过正则表达式来解析错误，非常麻烦。他还提到堆栈跟踪的重要性，以便在捕获和包装错误时能精确定位错误来源。

• samber 分享了自己编写的错误包装库 `oops`，该库支持完整的堆栈跟踪以及丰富的元数据添加功能，如时间、标签、用户信息等。

• darthbanane 指出 `WithMeta` 函数在参数不是成对出现时会引发 panic，认为这是 Go 错误处理困难的一个例子。

• gregwebs 提到使用现有的 Go 错误库，并推荐使用 `slog` 属性来复用日志属性，从而实现添加元数据的功能。

• sethammons 支持结构化错误日志，并分享了自己编写的 Go 错误包装工具 `kverr`，同时提到在 Python 中也希望实现类似的结构化异常处理。

• fastest963 介绍了自己使用 `errctx` 库来存储错误中的键值对，并实现了错误展开以查找深层存储的键。

• weakfish 对使用第三方库进行结构化日志记录持怀疑态度，认为应该使用 Go 自带的 `slog`。

• altbdoor 认为 Go 的错误处理有些奇怪，但自己主要是在小项目中使用，因此影响不大。

• vikeri 指出错误中缺少标记特定错误代码的功能，无法轻松地对相似错误进行分组，并询问是否可以通过 "tag" 实现这一需求。

• dedicate 提问，对于中小型项目来说，这种高度结构化的错误处理是否会带来过多工作量，是否值得。

• sigmonsays 认为可以使用 Go 内置的 `errors.Wrapf` 和 `slog` 来实现类似的功能，无需额外引入复杂的库。

• aor215 分享了自己几年前写的一篇关于错误处理的文章，并提到其解决方案在多个项目中得到了成功应用。

补充讨论：
• 错误处理中的并发安全性、性能代价和内存开销是争议的焦点之一。
• 使用字符串作为错误返回值的缺点被多位讨论者提到，推荐使用结构化错误或错误类。
• 堆栈跟踪和元数据（如标签、用户信息）的添加被认为是错误处理中的重要功能。
• 不同开发者对第三方库和 Go 自带工具的选择存在分歧。
• 对于中小型项目是否需要高度结构化的错误处理，讨论中提出了实用性和工作量的问题。

Structured errors in Go
Bridge the gap between structured logging and errors in Go
written
almost 3 years ago
This post documents a catalogue of experiments on the topic of error management in medium-sized Go programs, specifically HTTP APIs, with certain end goals in mind around ergonomics, syntactic salt and making the lives of everyone involved easier. The final result is a simple approach and a new library that I've been using in production for a couple of months now.
Error handling (or, more accurately, error
management
) has always ended up being a hot topic with Go. Most likely because of two things. Firstly, Go's early ideas about error handling – as with a lot of Go's design – chose to steer away from commonly found implementations such as exception handling and opted for a vastly simpler (at least from an implementation perspective) approach: return values. Secondly, the smallest, simplest form of an error in Go is a string of text. This leaves a lot of room for building on top of the simple concept of a string of text.
type
error
interface
{
Error
(
)
string
}
Every Go programmer is familiar with this interface. The beauty in simplicity here is that any type that satisfies this interface is an error. This allows us to construct domain-specific types that satisfy our needs if those needs stretch beyond a simple string of text.
Okay, so you know that. I did the one thing I hate in articles about some topic and described the absolute basics of said topic despite the fact that whoever is reading this already knows all of that before getting to the
actual
content.
Structured logging
(unrelated to lumberjack unions)
I won't do that here, promise. You all know what structured logging is. It's basically a standard concept in most medium and larger systems. As
Brandon Willett writes
,
Structured logs are non-negotiable
.
So what does this have to do with error handling? Well, first of all, let's define
error handling
by showing what it's not:

This is not error handling. Nothing about this code is handling anything. This is I-don't-know-what-to-do-with-this-error-so-you-deal-with-it.
And this is fine and this is still one part of what I call error
management
because there are a few different key events during the lifecycle of an error.

Step 2 is what we're interested in here.

Now, log aggregators are incredibly powerful. You can filter based on the service, the account that made the request, the trace ID, the filename that the log entry originated from, the region the service is running in, and infinitely more options. 这篇文章讨论了Go语言中错误管理的问题，特别是在中型程序和HTTP API中的应用。作者通过一系列实验，提出了一种简化错误处理的方法，并开发了一个新的库来实现这一目标。Go的错误处理通常依赖于返回值，而非异常机制，最简单的错误形式是字符串。虽然这种设计简单，但缺乏结构化信息。

文章强调了结构化日志的重要性，指出在错误管理中，错误信息需要被结构化，以便于日志聚合器和报警系统处理。传统上，错误信息是简单的字符串，难以进行有效的过滤和分析。为了改善这一情况，作者建议将错误信息结构化，例如在日志中加入"account_id"等具体字段，以便更好地诊断问题。

最终，作者提出了一种方法来弥合错误值和结构化日志之间的差距，并通过一个新库来实现这一功能，以提高错误管理的效率和可维护性。

data.title: Why Use Structured Errors in Rust Applications?
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了在Rust应用中使用结构化错误（如`thiserror`）相比于非结构化错误（如`anyhow`）的优缺点，尤其在错误传播场景中的应用。虽然`anyhow`在应用开发中因其简便性被广泛使用，但作者更偏好`thiserror`，原因包括：

1. **可读性和可维护性**：自定义错误类型能让开发者一目了然地看到所有可能的错误模式，无需深入函数实现，且有助于代码审查。
2. **一致性和简洁性**：错误信息只需定义一次，避免重复，且通过宏自动生成文档，提升开发体验。
3. **附加功能**：自定义错误类型可以附加功能，如序列化、关联HTTP状态码、本地化错误消息等。
4. **强制性错误处理**：`thiserror`强制开发者考虑错误处理，避免遗漏错误上下文。

不过，使用自定义错误类型也会增加代码量和复杂性，因此需要权衡选择。在库开发中，作者强烈建议使用`thiserror`以提供更多信息和可靠性。

44148708.article_content:
Why Use Structured Errors in Rust Applications?
Posted on
May 28, 2025
Last edited
May 30, 2025
8 mins
Error Handling
Tech
Table of Contents
TL;DR I prefer
thiserror
enums over
anyhow
, even for application code that
simply propagates errors. Custom error types require additional effort, but make
the code easier to reason about and maintain down the road.
“Using
thiserror
for libraries and
anyhow
for applications”
In 2025, this is the conventional error handling practice in the Rust community.
Let’s quickly recap the main ideas:
Libraries should expose error types that provide as much information as
possible. This allows the callers to detect and handle specific error
conditions. A specific error code is more useful than “Oops, something went
wrong”. Structured
1
error types facilitate statically-checked
pattern matching, which is more reliable than runtime reflection, downcasting,
or regex-matching an error message. They also provide nice autogenerated docs,
which is very important for libraries.
Unfortunately, propagating structured errors in Rust is associated with the
boilerplate of manually writing out wrapper error types, their
impl
s and
conversions.
2
thiserror
removes the boilerplate
around implementing
Display
,
Error
and
From
for your error
types. Using it is a no-brainer for libraries that can “afford” proc macro
dependencies. Although, you still need to define and annotate the wrapper
types themselves, which there are usually plenty.
End applications often don’t care about the specific cause of an error and
simply propagate errors up the stack until they reach some kind of a
“catch-all” point. For this use case, even
thiserror
-assisted error types
are often considered too cumbersome and not worth it.
Instead, application developers commonly use
anyhow
. It provides a “universal”
dynamic error type, along with helper methods that make dealing with it even
easier than returning a string.
3
If you google “error handling in Rust”, the typical introductory posts are going
to start with the basics of
panic
,
Option
and
Result
, then explain these
two libraries, give this rule of thumb to choose bethween them, show some code,
and stop right here.
Pattern matching isn’t the only reason to use structured errors
At work, my team has written a ~50k LoC web server in Rust. We’ve been
maintaining it full-time for over a year. It mostly follows the same pattern of
“just propagate the error” and almost never pattern-matches specific error
conditions. The main benefit of structured errors is not applicable. It sounds
like we should be using something like
anyhow
instead of spending time on
maintaining our own error types. But I found many other benefits of doing so:
Custom error types allow you to see all potential failure modes of a function
at a glance, without (recursively) inspecting its implementation or
maintaining fragile hand-written docs that can’t be fully trusted anyway. In a
code review, you can easily notice when some error variant doesn’t make sense
and should be handled locally, or comes from an action that shouldn’t be
performed at all. Interfaces become more descriptive.
When the error type is narrow and descriptive enough, you can understand the
function just by looking at its signature, without even going to the error
definition:
fn
foo
(
..
) -> Result
<..
, TheOnlyPossibleFailure
>
You don’t repeat yourself when the same error is thrown from multiple places.
Each error message is specified once when you define the type
4
. This results in a more consistent user experience, as
well as better developer experience. Now your domain errors have IDE
integration, with operations like “find references” and so on.
The logic is less littered with error messages or adding context.
return Err(MyType)
,
?
or
map_err
are usually more compact than full
error text formatting. There may be more code overall, but the error-related
code is moved “out of the way” to the type definition.
Although
anyhow
provides convenience methods for adding context to errors,
in practice it’s easy to forget, and
?
works happily without context. I had
to debug such cases multiple times. In contrast,
thiserror
derive forces you
to think about this, because you have to explicitly put
something
in the
#[error(...)]
annotation. Even if you roll with
#[error(transparent)]
(no
context), that’s now an explicit choice that can be questioned in a code
review, etc.
Custom error types can be enriched with additional data and
functionality
5
:
You can slap on
#[derive(Serialize)]
to log/return nested JSON data along with an error.
You can implement
std::process::Termination
to give your error an associated
ExitCode
.
You can implement
axum::IntoResponse
to give your error an associated
HTTP status
code
.
You can implement something like this to have localized error messages:
trait
Localize {
fn
localize
(
&
self, language:
Language
) -> String;
}
The tradeoffs
Custom errors have their drawbacks:
It’s more code and more types
6
.

文章主要讨论了在Rust应用中使用结构化错误（如`thiserror`）相比于非结构化错误（如`anyhow`）的优缺点，尤其在错误传播场景中的应用。虽然`anyhow`在应用开发中因其简便性被广泛使用，但作者更偏好`thiserror`，原因包括：

1. **可读性和可维护性**：自定义错误类型能让开发者一目了然地看到所有可能的错误模式，无需深入函数实现，且有助于代码审查。
2. **一致性和简洁性**：错误信息只需定义一次，避免重复，且通过宏自动生成文档，提升开发体验。
3. **附加功能**：自定义错误类型可以附加功能，如序列化、关联HTTP状态码、本地化错误消息等。
4. **强制性错误处理**：`thiserror`强制开发者考虑错误处理，避免遗漏错误上下文。

不过，使用自定义错误类型也会增加代码量和复杂性，因此需要权衡选择。在库开发中，作者强烈建议使用`thiserror`以提供更多信息和可靠性。
44148708.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust 中错误处理的有效性和不同方案的比较

不同观点：
• arccy 认为 Rust 中一些应用的错误信息缺乏上下文，比带有调用栈的崩溃或 Go 的错误链更糟糕，难以追踪错误原因和相关参数。
• lifthrasiir 提到 `error_mancer` crate 通过自动生成错误类型来使错误定义和函数相邻，认为这是一种不错的做法，尽管并非适用于所有情况。
• stevefan1999 建议使用 `derive_more` 而不是 `thiserror`，因为 `thiserror` 依赖 `std`，在 `no_std` 环境中受限。
• ozgrakkurt 主张根据不同场景采取不同的错误处理方式，对于库代码和不应失败的应用代码，只需回溯和错误类型枚举；而对于可能失败的应用代码，则需要完整的自定义错误设置，例如 HTTP 服务器中的错误转换。
• reynoldsbd 强调良好的日志/追踪纪律的重要性，通过在可能失败的代码前添加日志消息来高效定位问题，不依赖第三方错误框架，认为错误和上下文应分开处理。
• suddenlybananas 希望使用 `thiserror` 设置回溯更简单。
• oldpersonintx2 认为 `anyhow` 库虽然很酷，但使用起来感觉有点不舒服，像是在偷懒。

补充讨论：
• 错误处理方案的选择根据具体场景（如库代码与应用代码）有所不同。
• 对第三方错误框架的使用存在不同看法，有人认为其有助于错误处理，有人则认为其增加不必要的复杂性。
• 对 `thiserror` 的依赖 `std` 问题在 `no_std` 环境中受到关注，并提出了替代方案。
• 错误信息的上下文和可追溯性是讨论中的重要焦点，不同开发者对如何提供足够的上下文信息有不同见解。

data.title: Codex CLI is going native
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: OpenAI宣布将Codex CLI工具重写为Rust版本，以提升跨平台稳定性、安全性、性能和可扩展性。目前Codex CLI基于Node.js，存在一些依赖和性能问题，新版本旨在解决这些问题，包括实现零依赖安装、原生安全绑定和优化性能。开发者可以通过运行指定命令试用新版Codex CLI。团队将继续修复TypeScript版本的问题，并逐步使Rust版本在功能上与其看齐。未来计划整合TypeScript和Python等语言支持，并邀请社区贡献者加入。如有问题或反馈，可联系维护团队。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕不同编程语言、工具和生态系统的选择及其重写的讨论，包括背后的技术与非技术原因。

不同观点：
• [wiseowise, tptacek, pjmlp, ThouYS] 认为从解释型语言（如Python、JavaScript）转向原生编译语言（如Go/Rust）是一种回潮趋势。这种趋势的动机部分是为了提升性能和避免Node.js等工具的安装麻烦。有人认为Node.js从一开始就是奇怪的选择。
• [crop_rotation, adsharma, geertj] 讨论了Codex（由OpenAI开发的代码生成工具）与Claude Code的比较，以及Codex是否能自我重写。有人质疑Codex能否在没有人类干预的情况下完成重写任务。
• [quotemstr] 提出语言选择往往与其他技术选择（如内存管理、编译机制、工具集和类型系统严格性）混为一谈。他指出Go的垃圾回收机制表现不错，因此不能简单地说手动内存管理就一定比垃圾回收快。他还强调，语言选择不仅仅是技术偏好，还代表了开发者文化。
• [vendiddy, jbellis] 提到性能问题，特别是桌面客户端（如ChatGPT）的卡顿问题，认为性能优化是选择不同语言或工具链的一个重要原因。
• [CGamesPlay, light_hue_1] 认为OpenAI可能以Rust重写为借口，实际上是为了转向闭源策略，减少开放性。

补充讨论：
• [phito, npalli] 对JavaScript/TypeScript开发CLI工具表示怀疑，认为未来可能会再次出现大规模重写和改变技术栈的趋势。同时，有人警告说，未来维护大量Rust代码也可能成为新的挑战。

争议焦点：
• 重写是否仅仅出于技术需求（如性能、易于部署）还是为了非技术原因（如闭源策略）。
• 不同开发者社区对语言选择的强烈认同感和文化归属感，导致语言争论往往变得激烈。

总结：讨论反映了技术社区对编程语言和工具链选择的复杂性，不仅涉及技术性能，还涉及开发者文化、历史选择和商业策略等多重因素。

Hello! Thank you all for the excitement, feedback, and contributions over the past month or so since launch. It's been incredible to hear from all of you building with Codex CLI and now Codex in ChatGPT
1
Special thank you to all the contributors who opened PRs to improve the CLI for everyone. From fixing bugs to adding features, it's been a lot of fun co-developing this with all of you. We wanted to share an update on a few recurring themes: cross-platform stability, security, performance, and extensibility.
We're continuing to address feedback and fix issues that we hear from the community, while we've been working on a rewrite of Codex CLI into Rust. You can try it today by running:
npm i -g @openai/codex@native
codex
If you're a TypeScript developer like me, you're probably wondering why would we do this. High-level: we want to use the best tool for the job. While Codex CLI ships with a neat terminal UI, which has been easy to whip up and iterate with React-based
ink
2
- the core of this project is an "agentic" harness, aka calling the model in a loop.
Our goal is to make the software pieces as efficient as possible and there were a few areas we wanted to improve:
Zero-dependency Install
— currently Node v22+ is required, which is frustrating or a blocker for some users
Native Security Bindings
— surprise! we already ship a Rust for linux sandboxing since the bindings were available
Optimized Performance
— no runtime garbage collection, resulting in lower memory consumption
Extensible Protocol
— we've been working on a "wire protocol" for Codex CLI to allow developers to extend the agent in different languages (including Type/JavaScript, Python, etc) and MCPs (
already supported in Rust
)
We're planning to continue merging bugfixes in the TypeScript implementation, while we get the Rust implementation to experience and feature parity in the coming weeks. We'll share more updates soon on how TypeScript and other languages like Python will fit in long-term into this project.
If working in Rust, contributing to codex-cli, and building new modes of agentic coding is exciting to you - we're growing our team! Please reach out to us at:
codex-maintainers@openai.com
We're excited to hear your feedback on the new version of Codex CLI as we work towards making it the default experience in the coming weeks. Happy building!

data.title: Atari Means Business with the Mega ST
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
《Atari Mega ST：面向专业用户的计算设备》

Atari于1987年CES上发布了Mega ST，这是其首款针对专业用户的工作站级产品。Mega ST采用了低矮的“披萨盒”造型，内置720K双面软驱和可拆卸的樱桃轴键盘，质量可靠。虽然它增加了2MB或4MB内存，适合开发者和桌面出版，但整体技术规格与1040ST差别不大，仍运行于8MHz，且未配备内置硬盘。Atari将其与SLM804激光打印机捆绑销售，作为桌面出版解决方案，但因品牌形象和价格问题，销售并不理想。尽管如此，Mega ST的键盘和内存优势仍吸引了一些开发者用户。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Atari ST系列电脑的技术特点、历史影响、及其与现代计算设备的对比

不同观点：
• Aldipower认为Atari ST（特别是Mega STe）的MIDI功能和稳定性无与伦比，甚至超过现代设备。他强调了Atari ST没有系统更新或后台程序干扰，运行非常稳定。
• jlokier指出Atari ST有大量的C编译器选择（多达22种），并认为Atari ST在开发工具方面曾经具有很强的竞争力，但最终未能与IBM PC和x86架构抗衡。
• alexisread认为Atari ST在设计上有很多未实现的潜力，提出了一些硬件改进建议，如统一时钟、立体声输出、改进的存储设备和更合理的接口布局，认为这些改进可以大大提升其市场竞争力。
• pjmlp回顾了Atari与Amiga在计算历史中的地位，认为那个时代的家用电脑和独立游戏开发具有独特的魅力，现代游戏开发者很难体会到。
• msephton分享了自己使用Atari ST的经历，强调其在个人软件开发和游戏设计中的奠基作用，并将其与现代游戏开发成就联系起来。
• zabzonk对Atari ST的功能有褒有贬，提到其独特的GEM GUI和游戏体验，但也指出其硬件设计（如斜向功能键和糟糕的键盘手感）存在不足，最终选择了IBM兼容PC。
• ggm回忆了Atari ST在特定开发场景中的使用情况，如运行core-wars，并提到其CPU包装设计。

Announced at
CES in January 1987
, the Mega ST was Atari’s first attempt at creating full-fledged workstation for professional users.
There is some conflict as to whether these are called Mega STs or just Megas. I’ve seen both names used and even have seen labels with both names. I tend to use Mega ST as it is much clearer and sounds less like “Amiga”.
By this point, the timeline for the ST was:
1985: Original 520ST
1986: 1040ST with 1MB of RAM
1987: Mega ST
It makes some sense that Atari would want to take the ST upmarket. Both the 520ST and 1040ST were largely mass-market product and sold with a thin profit margin. In order to continue to grow as a company, a product with a bigger profit margin was definitely needed.
Unfortunately the Mega ST had some issues with both its design and its market timing that hurt its chances. Let’s look at the design first.
Subscribe for free to Goto 10 to get weekly retro computing content sent to your inbox.
Subscribe
Design
The Mega ST takes the standard ST and puts it into a low-profile “pizza-box” case with an internal double-sided (720K) floppy drive and a detachable keyboard.
The keyboard was actually rather nice with cherry key switches. Sadly it retained the rather large key sizes of the earlier ST models, making typos too easy. It also had the connection for the mouse and joystick under the keyboard, which kept things neat and tidy but was a major pain to connect in the first place. The low profile of the case also meant that the disk drive slot would bump into the keyboard if the two were close together.
Overall, I’d say the keyboard is a solid B+ and it is a sought-after keyboard today for its reliability. This keyboard also
works great with the Mega STE
and I’d love to get my hands on one.
Other case differences include a built-in fan and a built-in battery-backed clock that ran on simple AA batteries. The fan was probably not really needed, but it likely improved reliability.
Technical Specifications
As far as technical specifications, the Mega ST did not have many advantages over a standard 1040ST. Its main improvement was that it had a blitter chip that could move data in memory around fast, which was great for graphics processing.  The Mega ST was the first to include TOS 1.02, which was the first update to TOS in ROM and included several bug fixes.
Perhaps the biggest “innovation” was the RAM. The Mega ST was available with 2MB or 4MB of RAM
1
, an enormous amount in 1987. This much RAM was a game-changer for developers and desktop publishing.
Lastly there was an internal bus connector slot, which ended up not really being all that important. The only thing I know that used it were some hard drive kits that would provide a way to squeeze the hard drive inside the Mega ST case. This points out a problem in the case design: it was just too short and didn’t have much room for anything else to be in there.
It would have made sense for Atari to sell an internal hard drive upgrade for the Mega ST, but instead they sold a separate external hard drive, the MegaFile, that you could place under the Mega ST. Modular perhaps, but more expensive and messier than an internal solution that would also not have external cables or a power supply.
By far the biggest technical limitation was that the Mega ST ran at the same speed at the 520ST and 1040ST: 8Mhz. The blitter certainly could speed up the display operations of some apps, but the Mega ST basically ran everything at the same speed as the older and much cheaper STs.
Marketing
The Mega ST was often promoted in combination with the SLM804 Laser Printer as a complete desktop publishing solution for just $3000 to $4000. At the time this was touted as a full system at the same price as just the laser printer for a Macintosh.
I don’t recall seeing Atari specifically market the Mega ST to developers, but I suspect a lot of developers found the better keyboard and extra RAM to be worth the upgrade.
In general, I think Atari had a tough time selling such an expensive product
2
. Even in 1987, the Atari brand was closely associated with video games and inexpensive computers. Trying to use the Atari brand for more expensive computers aimed at businesses was always going to be difficult. After all, many business would definitely balk at having the Atari label on their desks.
My Experience with a Mega ST
Although I never owned a Mega ST, my Dad did have a Mega ST 2. Since he also had the SC1224 color monitor, I would sometimes use it to play games. I remember hogging his Mega ST to play Dungeon Master quite often. I also remember that the keyboard was really nice and miles better than the one

《Atari Mega ST：面向专业用户的计算设备》

Atari于1987年CES上发布了Mega ST，这是其首款针对专业用户的工作站级产品。Mega ST采用了低矮的“披萨盒”造型，内置720K双面软驱和可拆卸的樱桃轴键盘，质量可靠。虽然它增加了2MB或4MB内存，适合开发者和桌面出版，但整体技术规格与1040ST差别不大，仍运行于8MHz，且未配备内置硬盘。Atari将其与SLM804激光打印机捆绑销售，作为桌面出版解决方案，但因品牌形象和价格问题，销售并不理想。尽管如此，Mega ST的键盘和内存优势仍吸引了一些开发者用户。

data.title: Why DeepSeek is cheap at scale but expensive to run locally
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了AI模型在不同环境下的性能表现，特别是DeepSeek-V3这类模型在规模化服务时速度快且成本低，但在本地运行时却速度慢且成本高的问题。这主要源于**批量推理**（batch inference）的机制，以及**吞吐量**和**延迟**之间的权衡。

GPU擅长处理大规模矩阵乘法（GEMMs），一次处理大量数据比多次处理小数据效率更高。这是因为每次GPU操作都有一定的开销，且频繁的内存读取会降低效率。因此，推理服务器通常会将多个用户请求进行批量处理，以提高吞吐量，但这也增加了延迟。

对于像DeepSeek-V3这样的混合专家模型（mixture-of-experts），由于其结构包含多个子网络（专家），导致GPU计算效率低，必须依赖批量处理来提升实用性。这类模型在低批量情况下表现不佳，因此在本地运行时速度慢且成本高，而在规模化服务中通过批量处理能达到高吞吐量和较低成本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Deepseek V3 等大型模型的本地运行成本、性能优化及批处理的必要性

不同观点：
• ryan_glass 认为，使用无GPU的CPU系统（如EPYC 9004系列）可以有效运行Deepseek V3，成本较低且功耗低。他强调通过大内存和优化模型（如Unsloth Dynamic GGUF），可以在不牺牲性能的前提下实现高效推理。

• perching_aix 支持批处理推理的必要性，指出批处理可以通过同时处理多个请求来节省时间，但也提到这可能导致回复的变异性。

44149238.article_content:
Why is DeepSeek-V3 supposedly fast and cheap to serve at scale, but too slow and expensive to run locally? Why are some AI models slow to respond but fast once they get going?
AI inference providers often talk about a fundamental tradeoff between
throughput
and
latency
: for any given model, you can either serve it at high-throughput high-latency, or low-throughput low-latency. In fact, some models are so naturally GPU-inefficient that in practice they must be served at high-latency to have any workable throughput at all (for instance, DeepSeek-V3).
This tradeoff comes from the
batch size
the inference provider chooses for the model: not batching inference inside an individual request
1
, but batching inference across tens or hundreds of concurrent user requests. It’s a peculiar feature of transformer-based LLMs that computing a batch of completions at the same time is almost as fast as computing a single completion. Why is that?
What is batch inference?
GPUs are good at doing big matrix multiplications (GEMMs, or “general matrix multiplications”). Say you have a single token that you want to pass through a model (i.e. by multiplying against all its weights - other architecture details aren’t relevant). You express that as a vector that matches the dimension (or hidden size) of the model (i.e. 1 x the width of its big weights matrices) and multiply it through. That’s 1 GEMM. But if you want to pass ten tokens through in a batch, that’s still only one GEMM, because you can stack the tokens into one matrix (10 x the model dimension). That’s a
lot
faster than doing ten slightly smaller GEMMs. So an inference server implementation might look something like this:
A request comes in with a prompt
That prompt is pre-filled (passed through attention - we’ll see later how that can be batched as well
2
), forming a KV cache and a token-sized matrix (1 x model-size) that will eventually become the predicted token
3
That token-sized matrix goes into a queue
A GPU server pulls batches (e.g. of 128) off that queue, stacks them up into a 128 x model-size matrix, and multiplies them through the feed-forward model weights
The end result is then split into 128 separate tokens
The one for the original request is streamed back to the user
Assuming that token isn’t an end-of-sequence token, return to step 2 to continue generating the next token in the response
Note that
the server decides
how big a batch size to pull. It’s a tradeoff between throughput and latency. If you do no batching and just process tokens one by one, no user ever waits in a queue (step 3 above), so latency is low (assuming you have enough GPUs). However, if you do a lot of batching, latency is high because users will be waiting until the batch size fills up, but throughput will be much higher because the GPUs are being used more efficiently.
Why are GPUs faster at multiplying large matrices once than small matrices many times? Two reasons. First, there’s some overhead involved in issuing each command to the GPU, and one big multiplication can be launched with a single command. Second, each new GPU command involves fetching weights from memory, which can be expensive for large weights. If you run lots of small GEMMs, you can end up spending most of your time shipping weights in and out of memory instead of computing.
Why are some models tuned for high batch sizes?
Typically an inference server will have a “collection window” where user requests come in and are queued. Chat servers typically aim for 5-10ms, but very high-batch backends might go as wide as 200ms. If a new request comes in at the start of the window, it might wait the entire window duration before being processed
4
. When the window closes, all the queued requests are batched up (i.e. all the 1xmodel-size matrices are concatenated into a single 128xmodel-size matrix) and that batch is sent through the pipeline. Running a batch like this is sometimes called a “tick”.
As the explanation above suggests, you can run any model at any batch size. There’s nothing inherently about the batching process that would rule out some types of model. However, it is possible to build a model so GPU-inefficiently that it effectively
needs
batching in order to be practical.
Why mixture of experts requires higher batch sizes
For instance, take a mixture-of-experts model (like DeepSeek-V3 or supposedly the original GPT-4). You can get a strong model by training it to have hundreds and hundreds of “experts”: separate blocks of feed-forward weights, from which a routing layer picks a subset that’s used on each token. But a model like this is really GPU-inefficient. We can see why: GPUs want to do a small number of really big matrix multiplications, but if you have many experts you’re forced into many small multiplications. Unless you do your inference in batches, that’s going to mean low throughput.
Let’s think through how a “collection window” of 5ms and 200ms would perform for a large mixture-of-experts model. Supp

data.title: A Pokémon battle simulation engine
data.author: rickcarlino
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了pkmn/engine项目，一个高效的宝可梦对战模拟引擎，专为性能优化，适用于工具开发、嵌入式系统和人工智能等场景。该引擎严格实现原版游戏代码的帧精确性和兼容性，比Pokémon Showdown模拟器快1000倍以上，并经过充分测试和文档化。当前main分支有较多未记录的重大变更，建议等待v0.1发布后再使用。引擎代码用Zig编写，驱动代码用TypeScript编写，可通过GitHub发布页下载或自行编译。使用npm安装驱动时需注意兼容的Zig编译器版本。若要集成到项目中，需通过Zig的包管理系统添加依赖。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Pokémon Showdown引擎、其架构问题、以及相关技术实现和应用

不同观点：
• spondylosaurus认为Pokémon Showdown中的某些bug源于对游戏基础机制的误解或特定实现细节，并以"Assist可以调用不允许的招式"为例，认为这是一个错误的设计选择，且与"ReviveCats"事件有关。
• rickcarlino对帖子时间戳问题感到困惑，提到自己不可能在八小时前提交帖子，并对帖子突然获得关注表示不解。
• zzo38computer关注项目中的C API实现，认为虽然有不足之处（如不透明数据初始化问题），但总体上支持C API。同时提出对自定义规则、队伍验证等功能的需求，并讨论了双打对战中的特定情况处理。
• Areibman提到使用poke-env库进行强化学习（RL）和大型语言模型（LLM）代理的开发经验，并希望新的API也能易于使用。
• weberer指出该项目目前仅支持第一世代的机制，暗示可能需要更多代的支持。
• jeroenhd对Zig和TypeScript结合的开发方式表示兴趣，但对其性能和Zig编译器补丁的存在感到惊讶。
• glimshe赞赏项目包含C API并采用MIT许可，但对底层语言未作评论。
• anthk表达了对一个理想化的、简化的Pokémon对战模拟器的需求，希望能够避免练级过程，专注于对战体验。
• deadbabe提出在开发回合制对战游戏时，使用引擎帮助平衡各种数据和变量以避免主导策略的出现是否必要。
• littlestymaar调侃了Zig开发中的常见问题，提到编译器版本带来的困扰。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点可能在于Pokémon Showdown的架构选择和bug处理方式，以及这些选择对游戏机制的影响。
• 不同用户对技术实现的细节有不同关注点，如API设计、编译器问题、项目功能支持等。
• 用户对理想中的对战模拟器有不同的期望，尤其是对简化游戏体验和自定义规则的需求。

总体来看，讨论围绕Pokémon Showdown引擎的技术实现、功能需求和应用场景展开，涉及多个技术细节和用户需求。

Warning
This project is under heavy development
and currently the
main
branch contains numerous breaking
changes which may not work and which are not fully documented. Please
wait for the forthcoming
initial v0.1 release
before depending on this project (code from the
old
tag can also be used to experiment with a
more stable version of the codebase).
A minimal, complete, Pokémon battle simulation engine optimized for performance and
designed
for tooling, embedded systems, and
artificial
intelligence
use cases. This engine aims to be a frame-accurate and
bug-for-bug compatible
implementation of both Pokémon battles as defined by the original game code and the
Pokémon
Showdown
1
simulator which represents Pokémon battling as practically
interpreted online.
The pkmn engine is
more than 1000× faster
than the
patched
Pokémon Showdown simulator
code
when playing out supported formats in
compatibility mode and is extensively
tested
and
documented
. Note,
however, that the engine is
not a fully featured simulator
but is instead a low-level library
which can be used as a building block for more advanced use cases.
Installation
This repository hosts both the engine code (written in
Zig
) and the
reference driver code (written in
TypeScript
).
libpkmn
Binaries of the engine code can be downloaded from the
releases
tab on GitHub, or you can
download the source
code
directly and build it with the
latest
zig
compiler, see
zig build --help
for build options:
$ curl https://github.com/pkmn/engine/archive/refs/heads/main.zip -o engine.zip
$ unzip engine.zip
$
cd
engine
$ zig build --prefix /usr/local -Doptimize=ReleaseFast
The Zig website has
installation instructions
which
walk through how to install Zig on each platform - the engine code should work on Zig v0.11.0,
though tracks Zig's master branch so this may change in the future if breaking language changes are
introduced. Note that
due to a
bug in the Zig
compiler
, compiling with a version of Zig before
0.12.0-dev.876+aaf46187a
is recommended for performance
. Alternatively, building a version of
Zig from source
after having applied
a
patch
to revert
ziglang/zig#17391
will
restore performance while allowing modern Zig features to be used.
libpkmn
can be built with
-Dshowdown
to instead produce the Pokémon Showdown compatible
libpkmn-showdown
library. Furthermore, protocol message logging can be enabled through
-Dlog
.
The
libpkmn
and
libpkmn-showdown
objects available in the binary release are both compiled with
the
-Dlog
flag by default.
@pkmn/engine
The driver code can be installed from
npm
:
$ npm install @pkmn/engine
The driver depends on being able to find compiled Node/WASM addons in
node_modules/@pkmn/engine/build/lib
to be useful. When you install the package a
postinstall
lifecycle script
runs
install-pkmn-engine
which checks for a compatible
zig
compiler
(see earlier regarding minimum version) and download one to
node_module/@pkmn/engine/build/bin
if
it can't find one, as well as looking for (and downloading, if necessary) the required Node headers
needed to successfully build the addons natively.
If you have configured
npm
to
--ignore-scripts
you must either run
npx install-pkmn-engine
directly or build the addons manually and place the artifacts in the expected paths.
pkmn
To include
pkmn
, add it as a dependency in your project's
build.zig.zon
using
Zig's
Package Management
system
:
.
dependencies
=
.{
.
pkmn
=
.{
.
url
=
"https://github.com/pkmn/engine/archive/RELEASE.tar.gz"
,
},
},
Replace
RELEASE
with the tag for the
release
you wish
to use (e.g.
0.1.0
or
nightly
) or the specific hash of any commit. Next, run
zig build
and
copy the expected hash from the error message into your
build.zig.zon
alongside the
.url
:
$ zig build
error: dependency is missing
hash
field
.url =
"
https://github.com/pkmn/engine/archive/nightly.tar.gz
"
,
^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
note: expected .hash =
"
122056b93b403033cb7d9bed96a02c2eb8cc1275515976167726ada6eb4207e8ef8a
"
,
You must add
build.zig.zon
to the engine package to be able to import it in your
build.zig
:

data.title: An optimizing compiler doesn't help much with long instruction dependencies
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了软件项目中编译优化对性能的影响，特别是在内存密集型代码中的效果。作者通过实验比较了在不同优化级别（-O0和-O3）下，一个内存访问随机位置的循环的指令数量和运行时间。结果显示，尽管-O3优化减少了指令数量，但对于大数据集，性能提升并不显著，因为代码是内存密集型的。作者还探讨了另一个内存密集且指令级并行度低的链表访问例子，发现即使编译器优化，性能提升也很有限，因为瓶颈在于低指令级并行度。文章最后提到，若遇到性能问题，可联系Johnny’s Software Lab LLC获取帮助。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文章的实用性及其对技术问题的分析与建议

不同观点：
• solarexplorer认为文章质量不高，虽然提到了内存延迟对指令级并行性的影响，但没有提供有效的解决方案或建议，仅推销付费服务。
• MatthiasWandel提供了技术性反馈，讨论了在指针表中的求和操作可能导致的瓶颈，并分享了自己通过将奇偶数值分别累加到不同容器中实现加速的实验经验，但指出这种方法不适用于类似信号处理的算法。
• dahart虽然认为文章中的例子较为刻意，但建议可以通过将指针收集到数组中并按内存顺序处理来提高性能，同时质疑了文章中某些代码块（如"if (idx == NULLPTR)"）的必要性，认为其可能引入了不必要的指令和依赖。此外，还对图表的呈现方式提出了改进意见。

补充讨论：
• 关于图表的讨论：dahart指出文章中的图表在Y轴和X轴的处理上存在问题，认为Y轴应从零开始，而X轴的刻度应保持一致，除非有非常 compelling 的理由不这样做。
• 关于代码优化的争议焦点：dahart和MatthiasWandel都提到了代码优化的可能性，但角度不同。MatthiasWandel基于自己的实验提供了具体的优化建议，而dahart则质疑了文章中某些代码是否引入了不必要的复杂性。
• 对文章实用性的批评：solarexplorer对文章整体的实用性提出了质疑，认为缺乏实际的解决方案，而dahart则希望看到更多关于替代方案的讨论。

44149185.article_content:
We at
Johnny’s Software Lab LLC
are experts in performance. If performance is in any way concern in your software project, feel free to
contact us
.
There was a rumor I read somewhere related to training AI models, something along the lines “whether we compile our code in debug mode or release mode, it doesn’t matter, because our models are huge, all of our code is memory bound”.
I wanted to investigate if this is true for the cases that are interesting to me so I wrote a few small kernels to investigate. Here is the first:
for (size_t i { 0ULL }; i < pointers.size(); i++) {
sum += vector[pointers[i]];
}
This is a very memory intensive kernel. The data from
vector
is read from random locations – depending on the size of
vector
we can experiment with data being read from L1, L2, L3 caches or memory.
I compiled this loop with Gcc, optimization level -O0 (no optimizations) and -O3 (full optimizations). Then I calculated the instruction count ratio – instructions_count(O0) / instruction_count(O3) and runtime ratio – runtime(O0) / runtime(O3). In an imaginary perfect hardware, where the runtime is proportional to instruction count and doesn’t depend on memory at all, the graph could look like this:
In the above graph, an O0 version might have 10 times more instructions than O3 version, and therefore it should be ten times slower than the O3 version, regardless of the vector size.
Of course, real hardware is different. The same graph for the same loop executed on my brand new AMD Ryzen 9 PRO 8945HS w/ Radeon 780M Graphics looks like this:
The O0 generates almost 10 times more instructions than O3 version, but when the dataset is big enough, this doesn’t matter a lot: O3 version is about 3 times faster than with O0 version. So, the claim is (at least) partially true. Of course, being three times faster is something one should nevertheless appreciate, especially since very memory intensive codes like above don’t appear to often (but they do appear, e.g. the above loop is very similar to looking up data in a hash map).

vectorization training
for yourself or your team?
