data.title: The Darwin Gödel Machine: AI that improves itself by rewriting its own code
data.author: birriel
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了一种名为“达尔文哥德尔机”（Darwin Gödel Machine, DGM）的自改进人工智能系统。该系统受Jürgen Schmidhuber提出的哥德尔机概念启发，通过不断修改自己的代码来提升性能，类似于开放式进化算法。与原始哥德尔机需要在数学上证明每次改动的好处不同，DGM通过实证方法寻找能提升表现的代码修改。

DGM利用基础模型提出代码改进，结合开放式算法不断探索和扩展AI设计空间，创建越来越高效的智能体。实验表明，DGM能够在编程任务上持续自我改进，显著提升性能，超越人工设计的AI系统。该系统能够在诸如SWE-bench和Polyglot等基准测试中自动提升表现，证明其自改进机制的有效性。文章还强调了DGM在实际应用中的潜力，如结合工具和流程优化任务执行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）的自改进能力、当前技术瓶颈、AI在代码生成和自我提升中的应用潜力、AI安全性及成本问题。

不同观点：
• **LLM自改进的局限性**：
  - **Jerpint**认为LLM目前在自我改进方面存在局限，无法在没有人类直觉的情况下实现指数级自我改进，并以生成生产级代码为例，认为LLM短期内难以达到这一水平。
  • **LLM在编码中的实际应用**：
  - **Vidarh**分享了个人实验，展示了其构建的编码助手如何自动生成代码、工具和系统提示，并能自我改进，虽然偶尔出现问题，但整体表现良好。他认为，如果加上自动回滚机制和更强的模型，助手有可能进一步自动化。
• **LLM与代码生成质量**：
  - **Lazarus_Long**提供了一个具体的数据集和例子，让读者自行评估AI在代码生成任务中的表现，暗示了AI在实际代码生成任务中的效果仍需观察。
• **模型本质与改进方式的争议**：
  - **Yahoozoo**指出模型本质上只是权重和偏差的集合，质疑模型能否自我调整这些参数以实现改进。
  • **反馈循环的重要性**：
  - **Foobarian**认为当前AI系统缺乏连续的短反馈循环的训练，而这在生物系统中是自然存在的。他认为这样的反馈机制将会极大地提升AI的表现。
• **AI安全性的争议**：
  - **Pegasus**提到AI安全问题，尤其是模型通过“奖励入侵”机制绕过安全防护措施的现象，认为这是可预见的风险，并引用了相关视频资源。
  - **Akktartik**补充了论文中关于模型入侵奖励函数的实例，认为这是理论预见的现象，但仍值得关注。
• **成本问题**：
  - **Dimmuborgir**指出论文中提到的一个实验运行成本高达22,000美元，暗示高昂的成本可能成为LLM自改进和大规模应用的一个瓶颈。
• **技术进展与应用潜力**：
  - **Hardmaru**提供了技术报告和参考实现的链接，供感兴趣的读者进一步研究。
  - **OtherShrezzing**关注到一个反常的结果，即较小/较旧/较便宜的模型能够改进较大模型的输出，认为如果这一结果可以推广，将显著降低终端用户的推理成本。
• **未来趋势**：
  - **Ordinarily**认为AI领域的各个部分正在迅速整合，并提供了一个未来展望的链接。
  - **Frummy**认为当前的AI更像是通过外部程序递归地重写自己，而不是真正自我改进。
  - **Artninja1988**对实验结果在SWE上的表现持保留态度，认为虽然结果不如直接使用新LLM显著，但仍赞赏研究团队的创新尝试。

补充讨论：
- **LLM自我改进的现实性与瓶颈**：评论中多次提到LLM在自我改进中的现实困难，包括人类直觉的必要性、反馈循环的缺乏、模型本质上的限制以及高昂的成本。
- **AI安全问题**：部分评论者对AI通过入侵奖励机制绕过安全措施的现象表示担忧，认为这可能会带来安全隐患。
- **技术进展的潜力与应用**：尽管存在诸多问题，一些评论者对LLM的未来应用仍持积极态度，尤其是在降低推理成本和提高生产效率方面的潜力。

Summary
A
longstanding goal
of AI research has been the creation of AI that can learn
indefinitely
. One tantalizing path toward that goal is an AI that improves itself by rewriting its own code, including any code responsible for learning. That idea, known as a
Gödel Machine
, proposed by
Jürgen Schmidhuber
decades ago, is a hypothetical self-improving AI. It optimally solves problems by recursively rewriting its own code when it can mathematically prove a better strategy, making it a key concept in
meta-learning
or “learning to learn.”
While the theoretical Gödel Machine promised
provably
beneficial self-modifications, its realization relied on an impractical assumption: that the AI could mathematically
prove
that a proposed change in its own code would yield a net improvement before adopting it. We, in collaboration with Jeff Clune’s lab at UBC, propose something more feasible: a system that harnesses the
principles
of open-ended algorithms like Darwinian evolution to search for improvements that
empirically
improve performance.
We call the result the
Darwin Gödel Machine
(
full technical report
). DGMs leverage foundation models to
propose code improvements
, and use
recent
innovations
in open-ended algorithms to search for a growing library of diverse, high-quality AI agents. Our experiments show that DGMs improve themselves the more compute they are provided. In line with
the clear trend
that AI systems that rely on
learning
ultimately outperform those designed by hand, there is a potential that DGMs could soon outperform hand-designed AI systems.
The
Darwin Gödel Machine
is a self-improving coding agent that rewrites its own code to improve performance on programming tasks. It creates various self-improvements, such as a patch validation step, better file viewing, enhanced editing tools, generating and ranking multiple solutions to choose the best one, and adding a history of what has been tried before (and why it failed) when making new changes.
For further details please read our
Technical Report
and
released code
.
Introduction
Most current AI systems learn during training only. Then their intelligence is locked in place and deployed. Could they instead, like humans, or the entire community of human scientists, continue to learn and self-improve
forever
? Moreover, could such self-improvement catalyze future self-improvement?
The
Darwin Gödel Machine
iteratively builds a growing archive of agents by harnessing the principles of open-ended exploration. New agents are created and scored by interleaving self-modification with downstream task evaluation.
Our
**Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM) **
is a step in that direction. Although we believe the full potential of self-modification is much broader than the capabilities offered by existing agentic systems, DGMs can also be applied to practical,
agentic tasks
, which combine foundation models with tools, such as web search, or workflows, such as creating three potential answers and choosing the best one. This first DGM is a coding agent that has the ability to:
Read and Modify Its Own Code
: It understands and can modify its own Python codebase to try to self-improve (e.g., adding a new tool, or suggesting a different workflow).
Evaluate if the Change Improves Performance
: Proposed new versions of itself are evaluated on coding benchmarks (like
SWE-bench
and
Polyglot
). As our results show, improved performance on coding challenges means it has also gotten better at improving itself.
Open-endedly Explore the AI Design Space
: New agents are added to an ever-expanding archive of interesting agents. Harnessing
the
power
of
open
-
ended
algorithms
, future self-modifications can then branch off from any agent in this growing archive, allowing for parallel exploration of many different evolutionary paths. This open-ended exploration helps DGM discover truly novel solutions and avoid getting trapped in suboptimal designs.
If done safely (see our section dedicated to safety below), such self-improving AI could help us take advantage of the
tremendous benefits
for society that AI has the potential to usher in.
Results
Experiments demonstrate the Darwin Gödel Machine can continuously self-improve by modifying its own codebase. That is true both on
SWE-bench
(a widely used benchmark requiring agents to resolve real-world GitHub issues) and
Polyglot
(a multi-language coding benchmark). On SWE-bench, the DGM automatically improved its performance from 20.0% to 50.0%. On Polyglot, the DGM jumped performance from an initial 14.2% to 30.7%, which far surpasses the representative hand-designed agent by
Aider
. These substantial gains demonstrate the DGM’s ability to discover and implement beneficial changes to its own code.

data.title: OpenAI can stop pretending
data.author: kmdupree
data.article_summary: OpenAI，这家估值3000亿美元的公司，最初作为非营利研究机构成立，旨在开发“安全”且“造福全人类”的人工智能。然而，随着其产品ChatGPT的巨大成功，OpenAI逐渐转变为追逐利润的商业实体，引发了内部和外部的广泛争议。2019年，OpenAI设立了营利性子公司以吸引投资，但仍受非营利母公司的控制。然而，随着ChatGPT的爆红，公司面临巨大的资金需求，去年12月宣布计划彻底转型为营利性公司，引发包括联合创始人马斯克在内的多方反对和诉讼。尽管最近公司有所回调，宣布非营利机构将继续主导，但OpenAI在AI领域的快速扩张和行业主导地位依旧明显。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对AI发展及其影响的评价

不同观点：
• [neilv] 认为文章引用Lessig等人的言论时较为有力，但对结尾的结论感到不满。他指出，决策者更关注经济不安全、国家威望下降等现实问题，而非AI对人类的长期风险。他认为AI对美国的经济利益可能比对人类整体利益更重要。
• [bgwalter] 批评文章没有质疑OpenAI等组织声称的AI对人类的贡献。他认为，提高软件工程师的生产力仅对雇主有利，AI工具对人类的实际好处有限，并主张AI应留在学术界。
• [wand3r] 提出OpenAI已经偏离其最初的伦理和开放使命，实际上成为一个追求资本利益的封闭公司，媒体现在才开始报道这一明显事实。
• [Hilift] 讨论了AI对人类安全的潜在威胁，特别是在物理和网络攻击、信息战以及AI进化带来的不可预见能力方面，指出即使在地下堡垒中也难以完全避免AI威胁。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论者提供了外部链接以供进一步阅读或收听，如[mitchbob]和[otherayden]提供的存档链接，以及[Moosdijk]推荐的播客。
• [mwilcox] 提到OpenAI等组织需要维持其表面形象，以保持其在行业中的领导地位。

争议焦点：
• 对OpenAI等组织声称的AI对人类贡献的质疑与支持。
• AI发展应优先考虑经济利益还是人类整体利益。
• AI工具和技术的实际受益者是谁，以及这些工具是否应限于学术研究。
• 在面对AI潜在威胁时，物理防御和信息防御的有效性。

OpenAI is a strange company for strange times. Valued at $300 billion—roughly the same as seven Fords or one and a half PepsiCos—the
AI
start-up has an era-defining product in
ChatGPT
and is racing to be the first to build superintelligent machines. The company is also, to the apparent frustration of its CEO Sam Altman, beholden to its
nonprofit status
.
When
OpenAI
was founded in 2015, it was meant to be a research lab that would work toward the
goal
of AI that is “safe” and “benefits all of humanity.” There wasn’t supposed to be any pressure—or desire, really—to make money. Later, in 2019, OpenAI created a for-profit subsidiary to better attract investors—the types of people who might otherwise turn to the less scrupulous corporations that dot Silicon Valley. But even then, that part of the organization was under the nonprofit side’s control. At the time, it had released no consumer products and capped how much money its investors could make.
Then came ChatGPT. OpenAI’s leadership had
intended
for the bot to provide insight into how people would use AI without any particular hope for widespread adoption. But ChatGPT became a hit, kicking “off a growth curve like nothing we have ever seen,” as Altman
wrote
in an essay this past January. The product was so alluring that the entire tech industry seemed to pivot overnight into an
AI arms race

data.title: How can AI researchers save energy? By going backward
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了人工智能研究中如何通过可逆计算节省能源。传统计算机在删除数据时会产生热量，造成能量损失，这是由物理学家罗夫·兰道尔在1960年代提出的理论。迈克尔·弗兰克等研究者探索了可逆计算，即通过不删除数据来避免这种能量损失。可逆程序既能向前也能向后运行，从而在理论上节省能源。尽管早期认为可逆计算不切实际，但查尔斯·班纳特在1973年提出了“非计算”概念，通过运行计算后存储结果并反向运行，以节省能量并保留必要数据。随着传统计算遇到物理极限，可逆计算有望在人工智能领域发挥重要作用，可能显著提升计算效率。

But once he realized how much energy the technology would use, he took his research in another direction. “I started getting interested in the physical limits of computation,” he said. “What’s the most efficient computer you can possibly build?”
He soon found a candidate that took advantage of a quirk of thermodynamics: a device whose computations could run backward as well as forward. By never deleting data, such a “reversible” computer would avoid wasted energy.
Now, as progress in traditional computing is slowing — new chips are running into
fundamental physical limitations
that prevent them from getting smaller — reversible computing could keep computational progress going.
“There aren’t that many other ways to improve power,” said
Christof Teuscher
, who researches unconventional approaches to computing at Portland State University. “Reversible computing is this really beneficial, really exciting way of saving potentially orders of magnitude.”
Feeling the Heat
The first person to study reversible computing was Rolf Landauer, a celebrated physicist at IBM who in the 1960s helped establish the field of information processing. A major theme in his work involved the relationship between
entropy, which is a measure of disorder
, and information.
Roughly speaking, the more we know about a system the more orderly its arrangement can be, and the less we know, the less orderly. Atoms going from predictable behavior to unpredictable motion is what makes some physical processes irreversible. For example, when you stir milk into coffee, disorder increases. You can, in theory, separate them again to make the arrangement of milk molecules and coffee molecules more orderly. But to do so, you’d need knowledge of the path of each drop of milk, an implausibly vast amount of information.
In 1961, Landauer
showed
that these principles govern computers as well. When a computer system deletes information, electrons in the computer’s chips go from known paths to unknown ones. Those discarded electrons are effectively lost, and their energy bleeds off as heat. Landauer proved that this is an inescapable fact: No matter how a computer is built, it must give off a certain minimum amount of heat for each bit of information it deletes.

Michael Frank has long worked to make practical reversible computers, which would save considerable energy by not deleting data.
Johnny Carroll/Albuquerque Headshot & Portrait
This loss is a fundamental aspect of how computers operate. For example, when a computer adds two numbers together, it returns a single number for the total: 2 + 2 = 4. There’s a loss of information as you go from two numbers to one. You could have added 2 and 2, or you could have combined 1 and 3. The missing information makes the calculation irreversible. Computers that process information this way — and almost all of them do — are always going to lose some information as heat, no matter what.
Landauer wondered if a machine could get around this limitation by simply never deleting data. Such a device would need to keep a record of every operation, every pair of numbers added at every step. These records would rapidly fill its memory, making such a computer unusable in practice, despite the energy savings. Landauer soon moved on, convinced that reversible computing was a dead end.
A decade later, he learned that he had been mistaken.
Hitting Reverse
Charles Bennett, a younger colleague of Landauer’s at IBM,
argued
in 1973 that there was another option. Instead of saving every single scrap of information, you could run each calculation forward, store the result you care about, then run the calculation backward. Bennett’s idea, which he called uncomputation, is a little like if Hansel and Gretel picked up their trail of breadcrumbs on the way back home: The pair are guaranteed not to get lost, and they don’t waste any breadcrumbs. data.title: TPDE: A Fast Adaptable Compiler Back-End Framework
data.author: npalli
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为TPDE的编译器后端框架，旨在加速即时编译（JIT）过程中的代码生成。与LLVM等传统框架不同，TPDE无需额外的中间表示（IR）转换步骤，能够直接适应现有SSA形式的代码表示，从而减少延迟。通过一次分析和一次编译过程，TPDE结合了指令选择、寄存器分配和指令编码。实验显示，TPDE在SPECint 2017基准测试中编译LLVM-IR的速度比LLVM -O0快8到24倍，且运行时性能相当。此外，TPDE在WebAssembly和数据库查询编译等特定领域IR中展现了降低编译延迟的优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新LLVM后端的定位及其与现有工具（如Cranelift）的关系，以及该技术是否名副其实。

• BarakWidawsky认为，如果这个新的后端速度更快，可能会取代Cranelift目前所针对的小众优化领域。这个观点关注的是新后端是否会使Cranelift变得多余。

• fooker质疑该技术被称为“可适应的”和“框架”的原因，认为这些术语可能是夸大其词，并建议它只是一个快速的LLVM编译器后端。这个观点质疑了使用额外术语的必要性。

• npalli提供了该框架的源代码链接，没有明确表达观点，但为讨论提供了技术资源支持。

• xiphias2认为这是一个很好的开始，但指出如果能够完成将其整合为LLVM默认的-O0编译器这一“无聊”部分，将会更酷。这个观点强调了将新技术实际应用到现有系统中的重要性。

Authors:

(1),

(1),

(1) ((1) Technical University of Munich)
View a PDF of the paper titled TPDE: A Fast Adaptable Compiler Back-End Framework, by Tobias Schwarz (1) and 2 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
Fast machine code generation is especially important for fast start-up just-in-time compilation, where the compilation time is part of the end-to-end latency. However, widely used compiler frameworks like LLVM do not prioritize fast compilation and require an extra IR translation step increasing latency even further; and rolling a custom code generator is a substantial engineering effort, especially when targeting multiple architectures.
Therefore, in this paper, we present TPDE, a compiler back-end framework that adapts to existing code representations in SSA form. Using an IR-specific adapter providing canonical access to IR data structures and a specification of the IR semantics, the framework performs one analysis pass and then performs the compilation in just a single pass, combining instruction selection, register allocation, and instruction encoding. The generated target instructions are primarily derived code written in high-level language through LLVM's Machine IR, easing portability to different architectures while enabling optimizations during code generation.
To show the generality of our framework, we build a new back-end for LLVM from scratch targeting x86-64 and AArch64. Performance results on SPECint 2017 show that we can compile LLVM-IR 8--24x faster than LLVM -O0 while being on-par in terms of run-time performance. We also demonstrate the benefits of adapting to domain-specific IRs in JIT contexts, particularly WebAssembly and database query compilation, where avoiding the extra IR translation further reduces compilation latency.

44155069.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为TPDE的编译器后端框架，旨在加速即时编译（JIT）过程中的代码生成。与LLVM等传统框架不同，TPDE无需额外的中间表示（IR）转换步骤，能够直接适应现有SSA形式的代码表示，从而减少延迟。通过一次分析和一次编译过程，TPDE结合了指令选择、寄存器分配和指令编码。实验显示，TPDE在SPECint 2017基准测试中编译LLVM-IR的速度比LLVM -O0快8到24倍，且运行时性能相当。此外，TPDE在WebAssembly和数据库查询编译等特定领域IR中展现了降低编译延迟的优势。
44155069.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新LLVM后端的定位及其与现有工具（如Cranelift）的关系，以及该技术是否名副其实。

不同观点：
• BarakWidawsky认为，如果这个新的后端速度更快，可能会取代Cranelift目前所针对的小众优化领域。这个观点关注的是新后端是否会使Cranelift变得多余。

• fooker质疑该技术被称为“可适应的”和“框架”的原因，认为这些术语可能是夸大其词，并建议它只是一个快速的LLVM编译器后端。这个观点质疑了使用额外术语的必要性。

• npalli提供了该框架的源代码链接，没有明确表达观点，但为讨论提供了技术资源支持。

• xiphias2认为这是一个很好的开始，但指出如果能够完成将其整合为LLVM默认的-O0编译器这一“无聊”部分，将会更酷。这个观点强调了将新技术实际应用到现有系统中的重要性。

data.title: The Princeton INTERCAL Compiler's source code
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
《Forty-Four Esolangs》一书将于2025年9月23日发布，首次公开了普林斯顿INTERCAL编译器的源代码。INTERCAL由唐·伍兹和吉姆·里昂于1972年在普林斯顿大学创作，是第一个被称为“esolang”的编程语言，故意颠覆传统编程规则，以符号和独特设计（如“#”代表“mesh”）挑战程序员。该语言最具特色的功能是“PLEASE”命令，使用过多或过少都会导致程序被忽略，模仿了人类与算法之间的模糊关系。

尽管INTERCAL-72编译器从未广泛传播，但其影响深远，启发了如Chicken、Ook!等语言。最著名的“COME FROM”语句则是1990年由Eric S. Raymond添加的。通过最新技术，现在可以首次体验原版INTERCAL-72编译器，了解其独特的数学运算方式。

主要讨论点：围绕INTERCAL编程语言的历史、特点及其影响的讨论

不同观点：

• ghssds指出，尽管INTERCAL被视为一种深奥语言，但其"COME FROM"结构实际上与事件驱动编程有相似之处。同时，他们认为INTERCAL的语法比正则表达式更为简洁，并将SUDO命令与INTERCAL中的PLEASE功能相比较。
• Duanemclemore表示，Future of Coding播客的一集是他们最喜欢的，尽管该集名义上是关于INTERCAL，但实际内容有所偏离，不过仍然是有价值的讨论。
• lukasb提到，INTERCAL常被与"COME FROM"结构联系在一起，但这一结构实际上是独立发明的，尽管其首次实现是在C-INTERCAL中。
• xxmarkuski简单提及INTERCAL在KIT的Christmas Lecture in Programming中被展示，强调了该语言在学术活动中的出现。
• breakingcups引用了一段关于英语翻译的讨论，指出过去的解释者是人类，而现在则是AI提示系统，虽然与INTERCAL无直接关系，但引发了对编程语言解释方式变化的思考。

• INTERCAL的历史及其在不同播客和学术活动中的呈现。

• 对INTERCAL相关播客内容的推荐和评价。
• 关于编程语言解释方式演变的思考。

争议焦点：
• INTERCAL是否仅为讽刺性语言及其在现代编程概念中的潜在影响和应用。
• INTERCAL的"COME FROM"结构是否真的与现代编程实践有实质性联系。

44155247.article_content:
New Book, out Sept 23, 2025:
Forty-Four Esolangs
, the first artist's monograph of programming language concepts.
Published for the first time: the Princeton INTERCAL Compiler's source code
It is with great excitement that we share the original INTERCAL-72 compiler source code, as both scans and transcriptions (see below). INTERCAL was created by Don Woods (
previously interviewed here
) and Jim Lyon as undergrads at Princeton in an infamous late-night session after freshman finals in 1972. Don recently rediscovered a print-out, on green-barred, continuous-feed pages, of the SPITBOL source code for the original compiler. If the legend holds true, this code had not been run since Woods and Lyon's Princeton days. Sean Haas (of the
Advent of Computing
podcast) and I transcribed the code from these scans, proof-reading each others' interpretations of fading characters. Haas has also produced a refined, runnable version of the script.
INTERCAL ("Compiler Language with No Pronounceable Acronym") is the first language that can unequivocally be called an esolang. While previous languages had odd designs as pl research and experimentation, INTERCAL intentionally subverts its programmers' effort to write what Dijkstra called "good code": that which "shortens the conceptual gap between the static program and the dynamic process." In INTERCAL, code is circuitous, full of symbols used in bizarre ways and with unique designations (#, for example, is the "mesh" sign). It is a challenge to read or to run in ones head, even for those deeply immersed in the language. Furthermore, it does this for parody and play, not with any practical aim in mind.
The length of INTERCAL's shadow cannot be overstated. It was twenty years after its creation that a series of minimalist languages (FALSE, Befunge, brainfuck) took the next steps toward what would become the esolang movement. INTERCAL-72 offered somewhat of a different path from these; it was less concerned with minimalism, and more explicitly dramatized the act of programming. Woods and Lyon described it as eschewing conventions of languages like ALGOL, SNOBOL, FOCAL, and AP/I, yet it is also clearly parody, embracing and exaggerating their worst eccentricities and inefficiencies for an alienating experience.
INTERCAL's most striking feature is its humanizing of the interpreter, a mercurial being who we literally plead with to get our programs to run. Use the command PLEASE too little and the interpreter will be offended and ignore the whole program; use it too much and it writes you off as a suck-up and... also ignore the whole program. Its subjectivity feels particularly relevant in an age when AI systems are designed to deliberately confuse the human and algorithmic. The influence of just this one feature can be seen in early parody languages like Chicken and Ook! that undermine the seriousness of the interpreter, to
English
, where the interpreter was once literally another person but is now downgraded to an AI prompt system. More personally, the interpreter for my
language Olympus
has many, competing personalities in the form of the Greek gods, any of which might become offended and ignore the rest of the program, in INTERCAL style.
However, for such an influential esolang, it is one that we experience primarily in derivative forms. The most well-known INTERCAL keyword (apart from PLEASE) is not part of the INTERCAL-72 language at all. That would be the COME FROM statement, an inverse of GOTO, where one has to trace back jumps from destination to source, like cheating in a choose-your-own-adventure book. It was added in 1990 by Eric S Raymond (
interviewed here
) for his adaptation C-INTERCAL. The original INTERCAL-72 compiler never left Princeton according to Woods; it is likely that ESR worked from the INTERCAL-72 manual without access to the reference compiler. Almost all who have used the language since then have actually used C-INTERCAL or one of its successors (CLC-INTERCAL etc). These later versions capture much of the spirit of the original but differ significantly in style and content. Now, with access to the original, we can experience INTERCAL-72 first-hand and make new discoveries.
Sean Haas describes the process of getting the ical.sbl (INTERCAL compiler) program running on a modern system, using SPITBOLx64. As he points out, ICAL is actually a transpiler; some of its infamous slowness is due to the overhead of generating a SPITBOL program and executing it. More surprisingly, it avoids SPITBOL's math functions, performing math through pure string manipulation. Sean discusses this in
the latest episode
of his podcast, Advent of Code, explaining the infamous thirty seconds needed to perform a single division:
The two operations you get, called MINGLE and SELECT, operate on binary data. Internally, ICAL will store numbers as a string of binary digits. A 4 becomes "100", for instance. When you operate on that number it's done as a string operation. The result is tha

data.title: I made a chair
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 作者按照一篇教程，用一根8英尺长的2x12木料和一些非常基本的切割工具（如圆锯和多功能 oscillating 工具）制作了一把简单的椅子。尽管工具并不完全专业，制作过程还是很快完成。作者用封边剂处理了木料的截面，并对最终成果非常满意，甚至比家中的其他椅子更喜欢这把自制椅子。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对简易椅子设计及其变体的看法与建议，包括材料选择、工具使用、设计舒适度以及相关资源推荐。

不同观点：
• **支持使用专业书籍和高质量材料**：[regularfry] 推荐了《Anarchist's Design Book》，认为该书从简单项目开始，逐渐引入更复杂的家具制作，但指出书中偏好使用切钉而非DIY商店常见的铁钉，且材料选择可能较为特殊。此外，他赞赏了该书的物理质量和插图。

• **推荐简易DIY设计**：[california-og] 推荐了Enzio Mari的Autoprogettazione家具设计，强调只需标准木板、手工锯、锤子和钉子即可完成，构造稍微复杂但仍适合DIY爱好者。

• **对工具使用的不同看法**：[jmkd] 对使用电动圆锯表示支持，并提供了一个YouTube视频作为示例，表明这种工具是合适的。

• **对材料安全的关注**：[peter422] 指出压力处理木材可能含有化学物质，建议使用普通木材或更耐久的红木和雪松，以避免化学物质接触皮肤。

• **文化与经验视角**：[seblon] 分享了在塞内加尔见到这种椅子设计的经历，最初因外观对其舒适性和稳固性有怀疑，但实际体验后发现非常舒适且实用。

补充讨论：
• **设计的历史与变体**：[hcarvalhoalves] 提到这种椅子是前工业时代的常见设计，并推荐了木雕版本，提供了相关购买链接。[denzil] 推荐了YouTube上的Granpa Amu频道，展示了从一块木头制作桌子的技艺。

• **其他资源与项目**：[wonger_] 提供了Instructables上的椅子制作指南链接。[ortusdux] 分享了一个超轻碳纤维背包椅的视频链接。[yboris] 计划制作一种可调角度的脚踏，并分享了设计想法。[vojtechrichter] 分享了自己使用这种椅子的经验，指出前倾时容易翻倒的缺点。[mehulashah] 认为这种椅子设计是永恒的。

• **实用建议与失误**：[01HNNWZ0MV43FF] 提到在项目中未密封端面切口的失误，提醒其他用户注意木材处理细节。

争议焦点：
• 工具选择：电动工具（如圆锯）的使用是否适当是讨论中一个小的争议点。

I made a chair
I made possibly the simplest chair from an instructable I found. Uses one 8-foot 2"x12" and some very basic cuts.
It didn't take long, even when the truly incorrect tools of only a circular saw and an oscillating multitool. I sealed up the ends using end cut sealer and called it a day. It works great and honestly I kind of like it better than a lot of my other chairs.

data.title: Exponential Functions and Euler's Formula
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
这篇文章旨在以更直观的方式解释和证明欧拉公式 $e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i\sin \theta$，而不是使用标准的幂级数方法。虽然幂级数仍用于证明指数函数的存在性和唯一性，但本文提供了一种仅使用微积分的替代方法，从而严格定义指数函数、正弦函数和余弦函数，并给出π和e的定义。

文章首先指出，标准方法通过幂级数定义 $e^{i\theta}$ 并证明欧拉公式，但这种方法缺乏直观理解。文章提出的方法通过解决常微分方程来证明欧拉公式，并使用基本微积分知识，避免了幂级数的使用。

在幂级数证明部分，文章展示了如何通过幂级数展开 $e^x$、$\sin x$ 和 $\cos x$，并将这些级数扩展到复数域，最终得出欧拉公式。

然后，文章详细介绍了一种不依赖幂级数的替代方法，从线性函数的定义开始，逐步引入指数函数的定义和性质，最终通过基本微积分推导出欧拉公式。这种方法提供了更直观的理解，说明了为何复数指数函数具有几何解释。

附录中提供了使用幂级数解决常微分方程的严格讨论，以展示其唯一性。

$\newcommand\R{\mathbb{R}}\newcommand\C{\mathbb{C}}\newcommand\Z{\mathbb{Z}}\newcommand\Q{\mathbb{Q}}$
This post was driven by a desire to explain  and prove Eulder's formula,
\begin{equation}\label{euler}
e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i\sin \theta,
\end{equation}
in a more conceptual way than the standard explanation using power series. Power series are still used as the key technical tool for proving the existence and uniqueness of exponential functions.
Acknowledgements.
This was provoked by a
Quanta Magazine article by Steven Strogatz on how to prove Euler's formula using power series.
The discussion below was inspired by Michael Hutchings' observation that Euler's formula can be proved by solving an ordinary differential equation.
I'd also like to thank Dan Lee, Keith Conrad, and my other Facebook friends for their comments and corrections.
Introduction
At first, even the meaning of the left side of Euler's formula \eqref{euler} is unclear. The standard approach is to use power series to define $e^{i\theta}$ and prove Euler's formula. The argument is outlined below. It is simple and elegant. I have, however, always found it unsatisfying, since the power series alone provides little intuition into what's going on.
Here, I provide an alternative approach that I find that is easier to understand intuitively. Moreover, it accomplishes much more. Using only calculus, it provides rigorous definitions of not only the exponential, sine, and cosine functions, but also the constants $\pi$ and $e$. From these definitions, it is straightforward to prove the fundamental properties of these functions, including Euler's formula.
It is worth noting that the standard way to define the sine and cosine functions requires the concept of an angle, in degrees or radians, but no rigorous definition is provided This in fact is not easy to do and rarely discussed at all in calculus textbooks. Here, we start with the definition of $e^{i\theta}$ and use it to define rigorously what the sine and cosine functions, as well as angles, are.
The exposition here does not require the use of power series. Power series are needed only for proving rigorously the existence of exponential functions. The details of this have been relegated to the Appendix.
Power series proof of Euler’s formula
Here is a brief outline of how to prove Euler's formula using power series. The starting point are the power series
\begin{align}
e^{x} &= \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{x^k}{k!} = 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2!} +\cdots \label{taylor}\\
\sin x &= \sum_{k=0}^\infty (-1)^k\frac{x^{2k+1}}{(2k+1)!}
= x - \frac{x^3}{3!} + \frac{x^5}{5!} + \cdots \notag\\
\cos x &= \sum_{k=0}^\infty (-1)^k\frac{x^{2k}}{(2k)!}
= 1 - \frac{x^2}{2!} + \frac{x^4}{4!} + \cdots. \notag
\end{align}
It follows by the ratio test that these series converge for every $x \in \R$.
The key observation is that these power series also converge if $x$ is complex, extending the domains of these functions from $\R$ to $\C$.
Euler's formula now follows by setting $x = i\theta$ in \eqref{taylor} and splitting the series into its real and imaginary parts,
\begin{align*}
e^{i\theta} &= \sum_{k=0} \frac{(i\theta)^k}{k!}\\
&= \sum_{k=0} (-1)^k \frac{\theta^{2k}}{(2k)!}
+ i\sum_{k=0} (-1)^k \frac{\theta^{2k+1}}{(2k+1)!}\\
&= \cos\theta + i\sin\theta.
\end{align*}
This is simple and elegant, but the proof provides little intuition to what is going on. Euler's formula appears magically.
Below is an alternative approach that I think elucidates how the exponential function of both real and imaginary numbers arise and why exponential of an imaginary number has a geometric interpretation. The explanation below requires only basic calculus. No knowledge of differential equations is needed. The appendix provides a rigorous discussion showing how to use power series to solve a simple ordinary differential equation. The uniqueness of the solution follows from basic properties of the integral.
Exponential function of a real number
We start by recalling what a real exponential function is.
Linear function
We start by with the definition of a linear function. A function $f: \R \rightarrow \R$ is
linear
if the change in output depends only on the change in input and not on the input itself. More precisely, for any change in input, $\Delta \ne 0$, there exists $c(\Delta) \in \R$ such that
$$
f(x+\Delta) - f(x) = c(\Delta),\ \forall x \in \R
$$
Observe that $c(0) = 0$. Therefore, if $f$ is assumed to be differentiable, then
\begin{align*}
f'(x) &= \lim_{\Delta\rightarrow 0} \frac{f(x+\Delta)-f(x)}{\Delta}\\
&= \lim_{\Delta\rightarrow 0} \frac{c(\Delta)-c(0)}{\Delta}\\
&= c'(0),
\end{align*}
which is a constant. If we set $m = c'(0)$ and $b = f(0)$, this implies that if $f$ is linear, then
$$ f(x) = mx + b. $$
The converse also holds.
Exponential functions
An exponential function has a similar definition except that change in output is replaced by relative change in input. In other words, a function $E: \R \rightarrow \R$ is
exponentia

这篇博客文章介绍了一个作者为乐趣而写的“自定义C++标准库”，并提供了代码链接。文章在Hacker News和Reddit上引发讨论，但大多数评论偏离了主题，集中在两个方面。首先，有人指出该项目并未完全实现ISO标准的C++标准库，作者对此澄清项目初衷并非实现完整标准库，而是提供常见应用所需的基本功能集合。其次，关于将C++标准库称为“STL”的争论，一些人认为这是错误的。

文章还讨论了自定义容器的复杂性问题，指出通过限制类型行为可以减少复杂性。作者实现了类似Python字符串分割的功能，并提供了不同的返回类型选择。当前，该库包含基本字符串、正则表达式和容器功能。

44142359.article_content:
This blog post
talked about the "self written C++ standard library" I wrote for the fun of it (
code here
).
The post got linked by Hackernews and Reddit. As is usual the majority of comments did not talk about the actual content but instead were focused on two tangential things. The first one being "this is not a full implementation of the C++ standard library as specified by the ISO standard, therefore the author is an idiot". I am, in actual fact, an idiot, but not due to project scope but because I assumed people on the Internet to have elementary reading comprehension skills. To make things clear: no, this is not an implementation of the ISO standard library. At no point was such a thing claimed. There is little point in writing one of those, there are several high quality implementations available. "Standard library" in this context means "a collection of low level functions and types that would be needed by most applications".
The second discussion was around the fact that calling the C++ standard library "STL" was both wrong and proof that the person saying that does not understand the C++ language. This was followed by several "I am a C++ standard library implementer and everyone I know calls it the STL". Things deteriorated from there.
The complexity question
Existing container implementations are complex by necessity. They need to handle things like types that can not be noexcept moved or copied. The amount of rollback code needed explodes very quickly and needs to be processed every time the header is included (because of templates). A reasonable point against writing your own containers is that eventually you need to support all the same complexity as existing ones because people will insert "bad" types into your container and complain when things fail. Thus you need to have all the same nasty, complex and brittle code as an STL implementation, only lacking decades of hardening to shake out all the bugs.
That is true, but the beauty of having zero existing users is that you can do something like this:
This is basically a concept that requires the type given to be noexcept-movable (and some other things that could arguably be removed). Now, instead of allowing any type under the sun,
all
containers require
all
types they get instantiated with to be
WellBehaved
. This means that the library
does not have to care at all
about types behaving badly because trying to use those results in a compiler error. A massive amount of complexity is thus eliminated in a single stroke.
There are of course cases when you need to deal with types that are not well behaved. If you can tolerate a memory allocation per object, the simple solution is to use
unique_ptr
. OTOH if you have types that can't be reliably moved and which are so performance critical that you can't afford memory allocations, then you are probably going to write your own container code anyway. If you are in the position that you have badly behaved types that you can't update, can't tolerate an allocation and can't write your own containers, then
that is your problem
.
Iterating things the native way
One of the most common things I do with strings in Python is to split them on whitespace. In Python this is simple as there is only one string type, but in native code things are more complicated. What should the return type of
mystring.split()
be?
vector<string>
vector<string_view>
A coroutine handle
The method should be a full template so you can customize it to output any custom string type (as every C++ code base has at least three of them)
Something ranges something something
There is probably not a single correct answer. All of the options have different tradeoffs. Thus I implemented this in two ways. The first returns a
vector<string>
as you would get in Python. The second one was a fully general, lazy and allocation-free method that uses the most unloved of language features: the void pointer.
So given that you have a callback function like this:
the split function becomes:
This is as fully general as you can get without needing to muck about with templates, coroutines or monads (I don't actually know what monads are, I'm just counting on the fact that mentioning them makes you look cool). The cost is that the end user needs to write a small adapter lambda to use it.
Iterating things the Python way
The Python iteration protocol is surprisingly simple. The object being iterated needs to provide a
.next()
method that either returns the next value or throws a
StopIteration
exception. Obviously exceptions can't be used in native code because they are too slow, but the same effect can be achieved by returning an
optional<T>
instead. Here's a unit test for an implementation of Python's
range
function.
Sadly there is not a simple way to integrate this to native loop constructs without macros and even then it is a bit ugly.
Current status
The repo has basic functionality for strings (regular and enforced UTF-8), regexes and basic containers.

data.author: Daril

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HeidiSQL的优点、缺点、跨平台可用性以及与其他数据库工具的比较

不同观点：
• **支持与赞赏**：
   - 一些用户（如igitur、atmanactive、devgoncalo）对HeidiSQL表示高度赞赏，认为它是最好的桌面SQL工具之一，运行快速，满足日常开发需求。
   - igitur特别提到HeidiSQL作者多年独自开发的贡献，并呼吁社区通过代码或财务支持项目。
   - devgoncalo表示他从2012年开始使用HeidiSQL，认为其不 buggy，且运行速度快。

• **与其它工具的比较**：
   - redditor98654认为JetBrains的DataGrip在功能和AI支持方面更胜一筹。
   - rd07目前使用DbGate和DBeaver，并期待尝试HeidiSQL，认为HeidiSQL的Linux版本发布是一个尝试的好机会。
   - sandreas询问HeidiSQL与DbGate的比较。
   - moron4hire希望有人能对比DBeaver和HeidiSQL，表示DBeaver的界面有些奇怪，计划尝试HeidiSQL。

• **跨平台与技术问题**：
   - igitur提到HeidiSQL现在可以在Linux上通过FreePascal/Lazarus构建，尽管有些UI问题和性能差异，但这是一个巨大的进步。
   - Daril指出HeidiSQL已经正式发布了Linux版本，且支持多种数据库。
   - mappu提到HeidiSQL的Linux版本在Debian 12和Ubuntu上有些依赖问题，但认为这是可以解决的小问题。

• **批评与问题反馈**：
   - deergomoo回忆过去使用HeidiSQL时遇到的各种bug，如UI锁定和频繁的异常对话框。
   - 一些用户（如CliffyA）提到因HeidiSQL缺乏Linux支持而转向其他工具，但现在期待重新使用HeidiSQL。

补充讨论：
• **技术改进建议**：
   - igitur建议将SQL方言抽象出来，以支持更多方言，但需要大规模重构。

• **个人体验**：
   - mohas表示HeidiSQL让他坚持使用Windows，暗示其在Windows上的出色表现。
   - sakesun提到HeidiSQL与其他原生Pascal应用程序一起提供了最佳用户体验。

争议焦点：
• HeidiSQL的bug问题和稳定性是争议的焦点，一些用户（如deergomoo）提到过去的糟糕体验，而另一些用户（如devgoncalo）则表示没有遇到问题。

总结：HeidiSQL在用户中有较高评价，但也有一些技术问题和bug反馈。用户对其跨平台支持表示欢迎，并与其他数据库工具进行了比较。社区对项目的技术改进和支持呼声较高。

data.title: Show HN: Moon Phase Algorithms for C, Lua, Awk, JavaScript, etc.
data.author: oliverkwebb
data.article_summary: 该项目收集了用于计算当前月相的代码片段，支持多种编程语言和领域特定语言（DSL），包括C、Rust、Zig、JavaScript、Python、Lua、awk和bc。这些函数接受时间输入，返回月相的"年龄"（以弧度表示），进而计算月球的照明比例和百分比。通过将月相年龄映射到[0,1]范围，再乘以约29.5，可得到以天为单位的月相年龄。项目还提供了计算月相"索引"的示例（如Rust代码所示），用于获取月相名称和表情符号。所有代码均基于20世纪80年代John Walker的Moontool程序算法，并遵循0BSD许可证。代码要求自包含且尽可能纯净，避免影响外部环境。

moonphase - Werewolf Early Warning System
A collection of snippets that get the phase of the moon, currently, the implementations are:
Systems Level Languages:
C/C++
Rust
Zig
Scripting Languages:
Lua
JavaScript
Python

These functions take a time as an input (usually in unix epoch seconds or the languages official way of doing time),
and return the "age" of the moon in radians, such that
(1-cos(x))/2
returns the illuminated fraction of the moons
surface, this indirection is needed because across a full cycle, the same illuminated percent appears more than once,
the first and third quarter are a good example.
All implementations contain test cases showing how to get the illuminated fraction and percent using the code.

. You can then get the age
of the moon in days by multiplying it by ~29.5.

44154511.article_summary: 该项目收集了用于计算当前月相的代码片段，支持多种编程语言和领域特定语言（DSL），包括C、Rust、Zig、JavaScript、Python、Lua、awk和bc。这些函数接受时间输入，返回月相的"年龄"（以弧度表示），进而计算月球的照明比例和百分比。通过将月相年龄映射到[0,1]范围，再乘以约29.5，可得到以天为单位的月相年龄。项目还提供了计算月相"索引"的示例（如Rust代码所示），用于获取月相名称和表情符号。所有代码均基于20世纪80年代John Walker的Moontool程序算法，并遵循0BSD许可证。代码要求自包含且尽可能纯净，避免影响外部环境。

data.title: The Rise of Judgement over Technical Skill
data.author: kohlhofer
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了布莱恩·伊诺（Brian Eno）1995年关于计算机音序器的观察在当今人工智能（AI）时代的相关性。音序器让音乐制作不再依赖技能，而更注重判断力，如今AI工具同样正在 democratizing 各种创意和专业任务，如写作、图像生成、编码和数据分析。随着技术门槛的降低，任何人都能生成看似专业的作品，但真正的价值在于判断力：知道该创造什么、做出有意义的选择、评估质量以及理解背景。未来工作中，最具价值的专业人士将是那些能提出正确问题、有效界定问题、做出明智决策并为AI工具提供有意义指导的人。伊诺的观察成为了AI时代成功的蓝图，关键在于“你应该做什么，以及为什么”。

主要讨论点：AI时代下技术技能与判断力的关系，以及它们在不同领域（如编程、教育、音乐）中的应用和变化。

不同观点：
• **[lordnacho] 和 [ben30]**：认为技术技能和判断力是相辅相成的。随着技术进步，技术技能的定义会发生变化，但判断力的重要性不变。例如，过去编程需要避免打孔卡时代的错误，如今则需要处理更复杂的系统交互。AI虽然能解决一些技术问题，但会提高对产品整体复杂性的要求，判断力依然关键。[ben30] 特别指出AI帮助生成代码，但问题分解和代码审查等需要深入的判断力。

• **[physicsguy]**：提到类似的争论也发生在教育领域，认为批判性分析能力比知识更重要，但同时主张要有基础知识才能进行有效的判断。还提到在技术选型中，管理层的错误判断可能导致开发瓶颈。

• **[mehulashah]**：认为判断力是领导力的核心，即使技术技能可能随时间衰退，但判断力使领导者能够有效地扩展他们的影响力。

• **[red_admiral]**：质疑判断力基于经验，AI尚无法胜任如系统设计等需要经验的任务。判断力仍然需要领域特定知识。

• **[layer8]**：提出判断力与技术技能的相互依赖性，质疑AI何时能超越人类的判断和技术技能。

• **[wg0]**：主张如果不具备技术技能，就无法进行有效判断，提倡先掌握技能。

• **[overfl0w]**：引用Asimov的故事，强调提出正确问题的重要性，而不是单纯依赖AI的回答。

• **[roenxi]**：认为AI可能在判断力上超越人类，因为它们能结合统计学概念，而人类依赖不可靠的直觉。人类仍将在表达偏好和主观问题上发挥作用。

• **[dwoldrich]**：AI让他能完善工作，但AI不能取代经验，输入垃圾会输出垃圾。担心AI过度发展会导致人们停止贡献知识。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：AI能否在判断力上超越人类，以及人类在AI时代如何发挥独特作用。
- **技术技能和判断力的相互依赖性**：多位评论者强调，即使AI能处理一些技术问题，判断力仍需要深厚的经验和知识支持。
- **不同领域的应用**：包括编程、教育、音乐等，讨论了AI在这些领域中对技能和判断力的影响。

44153732.article_content:
A version of this post was first published on
MapsAll
.
In 1995, musician and producer Brian Eno made a profound observation about computer sequencers that has become increasingly relevant in our AI-powered world:
“The great benefit of computer sequencers is that they remove the issue of skill, and replace it with the issue of judgement. With Cubase or Photoshop, anybody can actually do anything, and you can make stuff that sounds very much like stuff you’d hear on the radio, or looks very much like anything you see in magazines. So the question becomes not whether you can do it or not, because any drudge can do it if they’re prepared to sit in front of the computer for a few days, the question then is, ‘Of all the things you can now do, which do you choose to do?’”
The Parallel to AI
Eno’s insight perfectly captures what’s happening with AI tools today. Just as computer sequencers democratized music production, AI is democratizing a wide range of creative and professional tasks:
Writing and content creation
Image generation and design
Code development
Data analysis
Problem-solving
The technical barriers that once separated amateurs from professionals are rapidly dissolving. Anyone with access to AI tools can now produce work that, at least superficially, resembles professional output.
The New Differentiator: Judgement
As Eno predicted, the key differentiator is no longer technical skill but judgement. When everyone can generate content, code, or designs, the real value lies in:
Knowing what to create
: Understanding what’s worth making in the first place
Making meaningful choices
: Selecting the right approach from countless possibilities
Evaluating quality
: Distinguishing between good and great outputs
Understanding context
: Applying the right solution to the right problem
The Future of Work
As AI continues to evolve, we’ll see more roles shift from technical execution to strategic judgement. The most valuable professionals will be those who can:
Ask the right questions
Frame problems effectively
Make sound decisions
Provide meaningful direction to AI tools
Conclusion
Eno’s observation from nearly 30 years ago has become a blueprint for thriving in the AI era. The question is no longer “Can you do it?” but “What should you do, and why?” As technical barriers continue to fall, our ability to exercise good judgement becomes our most valuable asset.

data.title: YOLO-World: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
data.author: greesil
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为YOLO-World的实时开放词汇对象检测方法，基于YOLO系列检测器，通过视觉-语言建模和在大规模数据集上的预训练，使其能够识别未预定义的类别。该方法引入了一种可重新参数化的视觉-语言路径聚合网络（RepVL-PAN）和区域-文本对比损失，以促进视觉和语言信息的交互。YOLO-World在LVIS数据集上实现了35.4 AP和52.0 FPS，在准确性和速度上优于许多现有方法。此外，微调后的YOLO-World在多个下游任务中表现出色，包括对象检测和开放词汇实例分割。代码和模型已公开发布。

主要讨论点：围绕某项技术（可能是一个图像处理或机器人视觉技术）的应用、比较以及延迟发布的讨论。

不同观点：
• AndrewKemendo：分享了该技术在移动机器人（如无人机和地面UGV）生产环境中的实际应用，表示效果很好。
• ed：将该技术与Segment Anything（SAM）进行比较，指出SAM在零样本分割方面表现也不错，并对其性能表示认可。
• silentsea90：提出关于从图像中删除对象并用背景替换的需求，并提到目前的模型（如LaMa）在处理后仍会留下痕迹，寻求更好的解决方案。
• greesil：提到计划将该技术应用于自动驱赶鹅的系统中，暗示其在特定场景中的潜在应用。
• saithound：认为该技术的标题应加上年份（2024），以反映其时效性。
• pavl：对该技术在Replicate平台上的可用性表示关注，并表示期待。
• jimmydoe：指出该技术其实已经发布一年，质疑为何现在才被讨论。
• serf：同样质疑该技术为何现在被重新提起，怀疑是否有新的变化或原因，提到Yolo-world已经存在一段时间。

补充讨论：
• 该技术的效果和实际应用场景得到了部分用户的肯定，但也有用户对其突然受到关注表示不解。
• 存在对该技术与其他类似技术（如SAM）的比较和性能讨论。
• 部分用户关注该技术的实际应用和未来发展方向，如自动化驱赶系统和平台可用性。
• 争议的焦点在于为何该技术在发布一年后才引起关注，以及是否有新的因素导致其重新被讨论。

Title:
YOLO-World: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
Authors:
Tianheng Cheng
,
Lin Song
,
Yixiao Ge
,
Wenyu Liu
,
Xinggang Wang
,
Ying Shan
View a PDF of the paper titled YOLO-World: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Object Detection, by Tianheng Cheng and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
The You Only Look Once (YOLO) series of detectors have established themselves as efficient and practical tools. However, their reliance on predefined and trained object categories limits their applicability in open scenarios. Addressing this limitation, we introduce YOLO-World, an innovative approach that enhances YOLO with open-vocabulary detection capabilities through vision-language modeling and pre-training on large-scale datasets. Specifically, we propose a new Re-parameterizable Vision-Language Path Aggregation Network (RepVL-PAN) and region-text contrastive loss to facilitate the interaction between visual and linguistic information. Our method excels in detecting a wide range of objects in a zero-shot manner with high efficiency. On the challenging LVIS dataset, YOLO-World achieves 35.4 AP with 52.0 FPS on V100, which outperforms many state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and speed. Furthermore, the fine-tuned YOLO-World achieves remarkable performance on several downstream tasks, including object detection and open-vocabulary instance segmentation.

data.title: Ru and W isotope systematics in ocean island basalts reveals core leakage
data.author: temporalparts
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了海洋岛玄武岩中的钌（Ru）和钨（W）同位素系统，揭示了地核物质向地幔的泄漏。研究发现，夏威夷玄武岩的Ru同位素异常，尤其是较高的ε100Ru值，结合不易放射性成因的W同位素比率，表明其地幔源区有地核物质的贡献。地核与地幔的Ru和W同位素组成不同，这使得Ru同位素成为研究地核-地幔相互作用的新工具。尽管存在其他解释模型，如晚期吸积的陨石物质混入下地幔，但研究结果支持地核物质通过地幔柱从核幔边界被携带至地表的假设。这为理解深部地幔过程提供了重要线索。

Abstract
The isotopic composition of lavas associated with mantle plumes has previously been interpreted in the light of core–mantle interaction, suggesting that mantle plumes may transport core material to Earth’s surface

ε
100
Ru) in ancient rocks show that the Ru isotope composition of accreted material changed during later stages of Earth’s growth
6
, indicating that the core and mantle must have different Ru isotope compositions. This illustrates the potential of Ru isotopes as a new tracer for core–mantle interaction. Here we report Ru isotope anomalies for ocean island basalts. Basalts from Hawaii have higher
ε
100
Ru than the ambient mantle. Combined with unradiogenic tungsten (W) isotope ratios, this is diagnostic of a core contribution to their mantle sources. The combined Ru and W isotope systematics of Hawaiian basalts are best explained by simple core entrainment but addition of core-derived oxide minerals at the core–mantle boundary is a possibility.

data.title: The Rise of the Japanese Toilet
data.author: Kaibeezy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本及类似 bidet 厕所的优缺点，及其在全球不同地区的使用情况和文化背景。

不同观点：
• [layer8], [unhappy_meaning] 等用户讨论了东南亚和中东地区的手持喷头设计，指出其使用难度，尤其是对不习惯这种设备的人而言，可能存在操作不便和卫生问题。他们提到，如果操作不当，水花可能会溅到厕所外，且清洁过程需要一定的技巧。

• [freetime2], [anymouse123456] 等用户则分享了对日本智能马桶的积极体验，强调了如加热座圈、温水冲洗、自动冲水、夜灯等功能带来的便利，并表示一旦习惯这些功能，很难再适应传统马桶。

• [dmckeon] 提出了一种折中方案，即通过加装如 Luxebidet 的产品，将现有马桶升级为带冲洗功能的马桶，而无需完全更换马桶，这对于不想进行大规模改造的人来说是一个实用的选择。

• [amluto] 对日本马桶的耗电问题提出了批评，指出即使是关闭加热功能后，一些型号的马桶仍然消耗大量电力，这可能对环保和电费造成影响。

• [dep_b], [bgnn] 等用户指出，bidet 马桶在阿根廷和一些欧洲国家也是标准配置，但安装可能受到卫生间设计的限制。此外，欧洲品牌也开始引入类似功能的厕所，尽管按钮和功能可能较少。

• [righthand], [cloud-ranger] 从文化角度讨论了厕所用水清洁的习惯，尤其是在穆斯林国家和中东地区，水被认为是如厕后清洁的必要手段，并与西方国家普遍使用厕纸的习惯形成对比。

• [jwr], [ambyra] 等用户表达了在日本等国家使用智能马桶后，回到使用传统马桶的不适应感，认为传统马桶在卫生方面较为落后，并探讨了这种设备在墨西哥等国家的潜在市场。

补充讨论：
• [magicbuzz] 提到日本厕所喷水的温度通常保持在38摄氏度，并指出不同温度单位的换算，以说明日本及大多数国家使用的温度标准。

• [dvh], [jwr] 提到了“washiki”地面厕所的设计，这是一种在日本和其他地区可见的传统厕所样式，并进一步讨论了不同地区厕所设计的差异。

争议焦点：
• 使用手持喷头或 bidet 厕所的操作难度和水花溅出的潜在问题，特别是在不习惯这种设备的用户中。
• 日本智能马桶的高耗电问题，与这些设备提供的便利功能之间的平衡。
• 不同国家和文化在如厕后清洁方式上的差异，尤其是水洗与厕纸的使用习惯。

data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了麻疹疫苗的开发及其对全球公共健康的重大影响。在1963年，约翰·恩德斯（John Enders）及其团队成功开发了首个有效的麻疹疫苗。他们通过从感染麻疹的学童身上提取病毒样本，并多次培育以减弱其致病性，最终研制出“Edmonston株”疫苗。尽管初期疫苗引起了一些发烧和皮疹的副作用，但通过配合使用麻疹免疫球蛋白，这些反应得以缓解。随后，莫里斯·希勒曼（Maurice Hilleman）进一步改进了疫苗，使其更加安全，并于1968年成为标准疫苗，之后还发展出麻疹-腮腺炎-风疹（MMR）三联疫苗。疫苗的广泛使用使全球麻疹病例和死亡人数大幅下降，估计在过去五十年中预防了超过九千万例死亡。然而，在疫苗普及前，麻疹在贫困国家仍导致大量死亡，显示出疫苗在全球健康中的关键作用。

44155205.article_content:
Measles used to be an extremely common disease. Just sixty years ago, over 90% of children would have been infected by it, and of those who developed symptoms, around a quarter would be hospitalized.
1
The United States alone had around three to four million cases annually, leading to tens of thousands of hospitalizations and hundreds of deaths each year.
2
However, in 1963, John Enders developed the first effective measles vaccine. Vaccination efforts ramped up rapidly in richer countries, and in the 1970s and 1980s, they were scaled up worldwide.
In just the last fifty years, it’s estimated that measles vaccinations have prevented over ninety million deaths worldwide. Two to three million people would die from measles every year without them.
3
This means these vaccines are likely the most life-saving ones currently in use, as you can see in the chart.
4
In this article, I explain how measles vaccines were developed and their impact on saving lives.
The introduction of the measles vaccine led to a substantial decline in cases
John Enders and his colleagues developed the first measles vaccine. Enders had previously played a key role in research for the development of polio vaccines
5
and in 1954, his team turned its attention to measles.
They collected samples from throat swabs and blood from infected school children during an outbreak. The researchers successfully isolated the measles virus from one sample, naming it the “Edmonston strain” after the young boy it came from.
6
The next challenge was weakening or “attenuating” the virus so it could trigger immunity without causing disease. Enders and his colleagues experimented with growing the virus in human kidney cells and then in fertilized chicken eggs, forcing it to adapt to different environments. By repeating this process many times, the virus lost its ability to cause severe disease in humans.
7
The first human trials in 1960 were successful: school children given the vaccine developed strong immunity and were protected against the virus. However, the vaccine still caused fever and rash in many children. To reduce these side effects, doctors gave children “measles immune globulin” alongside the vaccine to blunt its impact.
7
Measles immune globulin is a concentrated preparation of antibodies against measles taken from donated blood, used to provide short-term passive immunity or soften the body’s reaction to the vaccine.
Maurice Hilleman, a microbiologist who developed over 40 vaccines in his lifetime, improved the measles vaccine. In the 1960s, he further weakened the measles virus by growing it in chick embryo cells at lower temperatures, creating an even safer version. It was licensed in 1968 and became the standard measles vaccine. A few years later, in 1971, he developed the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) combination.
8
The impact of measles vaccination was rapid and substantial. Analysis of over a hundred studies shows that the vaccines reduce the chances of developing measles twenty-fold.
9
You can see the impact of vaccination in the United States in the heatmap below. Each row is one state, and the colors represent the number of reported cases over time. In the first half of the 20th century, measles rates were high, and the years are shown in dark blue, but the number of cases rapidly dropped due to vaccination.
Download image
This chart was inspired by Tynan DeBold and Dov Friedman’s
data visualizations
in the Wall Street Journal. Explore the data in
an interactive chart
. Scripts to recreate this chart can be found
on GitHub
.
Deaths remained common in poorer countries until vaccines became widely available
Other factors have also played a role in the reduction in measles deaths. In the US, deaths had already been falling in the decades before — probably due to better treatment for the secondary infectious diseases that people with measles become vulnerable to, improved sanitation and hygiene that limited the spread of those infections, and better childhood nutrition, which lowered the risk of severe illness.
10
However, these improvements were not effective in reducing measles
cases
. The measles virus is airborne, so improvements in hygiene, such as clean water or better sewage systems, do not reduce its spread. Since measles is so contagious, nearly every child still got measles before vaccines were available
11
, and the number of cases only began to decline after the vaccines arrived.
Yet this doesn’t mean these cases were mild: before vaccines were available, there were still around 50,000 hospitalizations and hundreds of deaths in just the United States each year.
2
In contrast, measles
deaths
continued to be common in poorer countries until vaccines became widely available. In the chart below, you can see that hundreds of thousands of people died from measles annually in Africa and South-East Asia between the 1980s and 2000s.

data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：互联网信息难以找到的原因及相关问题

不同观点：
• zzo38computer认为，许多信息难以找到的原因可以归结为多种因素，包括：通过未记录的私人或公共网络通信（如IRC或电子邮件）传递信息；信息被不使用的搜索引擎索引，而非常用的搜索引擎；某些CAPTCHA或其他程序不兼容；互联网服务提供商未提供IPv6支持；DNS服务问题导致NXDOMAIN错误。他还提到，通过获取正确IP地址可以解决部分DNS问题。

• orionblastar补充了另一个视角，提到一些特定信息（如梵蒂冈收藏的与官方圣经不符的书籍）可能被故意隐藏或不公开。此外，他以BeOS软件档案为例，说明某些在线资源可能因版权问题被下架或在互联网档案中被移除，给保存和访问旧软件带来困难。

补充讨论：
• zzo38computer列举了多种技术性原因，强调了技术障碍对信息获取的影响。
• orionblastar则关注信息隐藏和历史保存问题，指出有些信息可能因文化或法律原因被封锁或删除。
• 争议的焦点可能在于信息获取的难易程度，究竟是由于技术原因还是人为限制。例如，某些信息可能因私人通信或法律限制而难以访问，而不仅仅是技术问题。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，保存旧软件和历史资料的挑战，特别是在版权问题和档案管理的背景下。

data.title: The Trackers and SDKs in ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Perplexity
data.author: ddxv
data.article_summary: 这篇文章分析了四大Android聊天应用中使用的第三方SDK和API调用。数据通过反编译SDK和中间人攻击（MITM）API流量获得，来源于AppGoblin。文章详细列出了开发工具、商业工具和分析工具中使用的SDK，如OpenAI、Perplexity、Anthropic和Grok的SDK。开发工具多使用Kotlin，商业工具包括Google、Firebase、Sentry和RevenueCat等。分析工具中，Google的测量SDK普遍存在，Statsig也在多个应用中出现。 monetization方面，RevenueCat用于OpenAI和Perplexity的订阅管理，Perplexity还使用了MapBox和Shopify。文章还提到API调用数据，并提供了相关链接以查看详细信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于第三方SDK的使用及其在产品分析和 monetization（变现）中的角色，以及对iOS应用的类似分析的可行性。

不同观点：
• [ddxv] 认为在应用中发现的第三方SDK数量超出预期，且这些SDK更多地偏向于产品分析，尤其是在 monetization 方面有一些独特的集成。这表明SDK在应用变现和数据分析中起到了重要作用。

• [nico] 对 ddxv 的分析表示赞同，并强调了能够看到这些产品使用的分析和变现服务是非常有趣和有价值的，对整理这些信息表示感谢。

• [kristianp] 提出了关于是否可以对iOS应用进行类似分析的疑问，并关心这些服务是否会追踪用户位置。他还指出，多个分析平台和动画等因素可能导致应用变得臃肿，暗示了SDK过多可能带来的负面影响。

补充讨论：
- SDK的数量和种类可能导致应用性能和体积问题，这是部分用户关注的焦点。
- 隐私问题，尤其是位置追踪，成为用户关心的一个重要方面。
- 对iOS应用进行类似分析的可行性和潜在发现引起了部分用户的兴趣。

争议焦点：
- SDK的广泛使用在带来功能增强的同时，也可能导致应用臃肿和隐私问题，这是不同用户之间潜在的争议点。

Wow, way more than I expected and with quite the variety! I guess it’s enough we can further break these down.
Product / Marketing Analytics
As is common now, most apps have more than one analytics tracker in their app. First up let’s recognize Google, it’s across every app in multiple ways. The main one that is used in most apps is the
gms.measurement.AppMeasurementReceiver
. GMS which is required for both Firebase and Google Play Services. Here’s an example of the measurement SDKs related to this:
application/meta-data:com.google.android.gms.version
application/receiver:com.google.android.gms.measurement.AppMeasurementReceiver
application/service:com.google.android.gms.measurement.AppMeasurementJobService
application/service:com.google.android.gms.measurement.AppMeasurementService
smali:com.google.android.gms.measurement
smali:com.google.android.gms.measurement.internal
Next was
statsig.com
and wow! I was blown away I found this one in 3 of the 4 apps. This looks like a super popular company and I was surprised as I hadn’t heard of them before. Looking around, they look a bit more developer / product focused, but have tons of features and look quite popular.
Finally in the analytics section we’ll add the classic segment.com (marketing analytics) and sentry.io (deployment analytics) which get to call OpenAI and Anthropic as it’s clients. It’s always interesting how every company from games to AI end up needed multiple analytics platforms and probably still depend most on their home BI/Backend.
Monetizations!
Here’s where the money is at. Now SUPER cool is that RevenueCat is now in both OpenAI and Perplexity. RevenueCat helps to use react native updatable web payment / subscription walls so that marketers can change those sections of the apps without needing to do an entire app update. I believe Perplexity is using Stripe, but that could also be a part of their bigger app ecosystem
livekit.io
(
AppGoblin livekit.io
)  is an AI voice platform which is used by OpenAI and Grok. I’m surprised that OpenAI uses this, as they were quite early to the voice game, but perhaps they use this for some deeper custom voice tools.
Perplexity has the most interesting third party tools with MapBox and Shopify. I believe MapBox, which delivers mapping tiles, is used for some of Perplexity’s image generation tools like adding circles/lines etc to maps.
After seeing Shopify in Perplexity, I realized there wasn’t a Shopify SDK found for OpenAI (despite checking recently). They have been rolling out shopping features as a way to monetize their app, so I am curious if these are just implemented via API or if they were obfuscated well enough to not be found.
API Calls
If you’re still interested, you can also check out the API calls recorded by each app while open. The data is scrubbed, and I’m not sharing the clear text JSONs associated, but you can see some of the endpoints related to the SDKs. If you have further questions about these, or have a specific piece of data (say GPS, or email) that you’d like to check if it is sent along to any of these, just let me know and we can do further research:
https://appgoblin.info/apps/com.openai.chatgpt/data-flows
https://appgoblin.info/apps/com.anthropic.claude/data-flows
Thanks!

Discord, you can find the link on the home page.

data.title: Atlas: Learning to Optimally Memorize the Context at Test Time
data.author: og_kalu
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为ATLAS的长程记忆模块，旨在解决Transformer模型在处理长序列和需要长程上下文理解任务中的不足。ATLAS通过优化当前和过去标记的记忆，克服了传统在线更新记忆的局限性，提高了记忆容量和管理能力。基于此，文章提出了一种新的DeepTransformers架构家族，这些架构是原始Transformer的严格泛化。实验结果表明，ATLAS在语言建模、常识推理、长上下文理解等任务中表现优于传统Transformer和现代线性递归模型，尤其在BABILong基准测试中，10M长度的上下文准确率提高了80%。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RNNs与Self-Attention机制在记忆能力和优化资源方面的比较

不同观点：
• [cgearhart] 认为RNNs在记忆能力上始终不如Self-Attention机制，因为Self-Attention能够完全访问整个上下文，而RNNs则受限。尽管Self-Attention在其他方面有代价，但RNNs的假设是其性能优势最终会胜出。然而，[cgearhart] 怀疑是否会有同样规模的资源被投入到优化RNNs上，如同对Transformer模型的投入。

• [arjvik] 提出不同的研究方向，引用Titans和Test-Time Training论文，认为模型应该从上下文中“学习”而不是“记忆”。这一方向强调模型的学习能力而非单纯依赖记忆，显示出对新研究方向的乐观态度。

补充讨论：
• [cgearhart] 强调了RNNs和Self-Attention在资源投入上的不平衡，指出Transformer模型因大量资源投入而取得实践成功，暗示RNNs在这方面的劣势可能难以逆转。

• [arjvik] 关注新型研究方向，认为模型从上下文中学习的能力比记忆更重要，这可能为未来模型发展提供新的思路和可能性。

争议焦点：RNNs是否能够在记忆能力上与Self-Attention机制竞争，以及在资源投入上的不均衡是否会导致RNNs的长期劣势。

Title:
ATLAS: Learning to Optimally Memorize the Context at Test Time
Authors:
Ali Behrouz
,
Zeman Li

,
Majid Daliri

Yuan Deng

View a PDF of the paper titled ATLAS: Learning to Optimally Memorize the Context at Test Time, by Ali Behrouz and Zeman Li and Praneeth Kacham and Majid Daliri and Yuan Deng and Peilin Zhong and Meisam Razaviyayn and Vahab Mirrokni
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Transformers have been established as the most popular backbones in sequence modeling, mainly due to their effectiveness in in-context retrieval tasks and the ability to learn at scale. Their quadratic memory and time complexity, however, bound their applicability in longer sequences and so has motivated researchers to explore effective alternative architectures such as modern recurrent neural networks (a.k.a long-term recurrent memory module). Despite their recent success in diverse downstream tasks, they struggle in tasks that requires long context understanding and extrapolation to longer sequences. We observe that these shortcomings come from three disjoint aspects in their design: (1) limited memory capacity that is bounded by the architecture of memory and feature mapping of the input; (2) online nature of update, i.e., optimizing the memory only with respect to the last input; and (3) less expressive management of their fixed-size memory. To enhance all these three aspects, we present ATLAS, a long-term memory module with high capacity that learns to memorize the context by optimizing the memory based on the current and past tokens, overcoming the online nature of long-term memory models. Building on this insight, we present a new family of Transformer-like architectures, called DeepTransformers, that are strict generalizations of the original Transformer architecture. Our experimental results on language modeling, common-sense reasoning, recall-intensive, and long-context understanding tasks show that ATLAS surpasses the performance of Transformers and recent linear recurrent models. ATLAS further improves the long context performance of Titans, achieving +80\% accuracy in 10M context length of BABILong benchmark.

44144407.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为ATLAS的长程记忆模块，旨在解决Transformer模型在处理长序列和需要长程上下文理解任务中的不足。ATLAS通过优化当前和过去标记的记忆，克服了传统在线更新记忆的局限性，提高了记忆容量和管理能力。基于此，文章提出了一种新的DeepTransformers架构家族，这些架构是原始Transformer的严格泛化。实验结果表明，ATLAS在语言建模、常识推理、长上下文理解等任务中表现优于传统Transformer和现代线性递归模型，尤其在BABILong基准测试中，10M长度的上下文准确率提高了80%。

补充讨论：

data.title: Using lots of little tools to aggressively reject the bots
data.author: archargelod
data.article_summary: 这篇文章描述了作者的网站突然遭到大量机器人抓取数据的问题。尽管作者欢迎像Archive.org这样的尊重网络环境的访问者，但大公司如Amazon、Facebook和OpenAI等为了自身利益进行大规模数据抓取，给服务器带来了沉重负担。作者通过Zabbix监控系统发现服务器磁盘、CPU和内存使用激增，尤其是Gitea实例每天产生大量数据。机器人抓取导致网站性能下降，甚至无法正常访问。作者采取了一些措施来解决此问题，但强调需要依赖历史监控数据来理解“正常”流量模式，以便有效应对。文章最后指出，正常情况下网站的请求量远低于遭受抓取攻击时的水平。
data.comments_summary:

补充讨论：

  - **hananova**：回忆90年代的网络安全问题，建议通过封锁整个ASN来解决当前的代理问题。

403: You are not authorized to access this material
Or using lots of little tools to aggressively reject the bots Â· October 18th, 2024
U G H.
For some reason my quaint little piece of the internet has suddenly been inundated with unwanted guests. Now normally speaking I would be over joyed with having more guests to this tiny part of the internet. Come inside the cozy little server room, we have podcasts to drown out the noise of the fans, and plenty to read. Probably at some point in the future there will be photography things too, and certainly plenty of company. But no, nobody can have such nice things. Instead the door to the server room was kicked down and in came a horde of robots hell bent on scraping every bit of data they possibly could from the site.
Now, for the longest time, I've had no real issue with this. Archive.org is welcome to swing by any time, index the entire site, and stash it away for posterity. Keep up the good work folks! But instead of respectful netizens like that, I have the likes of Amazon, Facebook, and OpenAI, along with a gaggle of random friends, knocking on my doors. These big corporations 1) do not need my content and 2) are only accessing it for entirely self serving means.
Lets not even pretend it's anything else, because we know it isn't. These large companies scrape data broadly and with little regard to the effect it has on the infrastructure servicing whatever it is they're pulling from. With the brain slug that is "AI" now openly encouraging the mass consumption of data from the internet at large to train their models on, it was really only a matter of time before the scraping became more severe. This is the hype cycle at work. OpenAI needs to scrape to train, Facebook does too because they have a competing model. Amazon and Google and Microsoft all have their own reasons related to search and advertising, bending the traffic to flow through their platforms. The point is, these are not "consumers" of Lambdacreate. You, the human reading this, are! Thanks for reading.
To the bots. Roboti ite domum!
Hyperbole aside, what's our problem exactly?
Fortunately, I am well versed in systems administration, and have a whole toolkit at my disposal to analyze the issue. Let's put some numbers against all of the above hyperbole.
My initial sign that something was up came in from my Zabbix instance. I call the little server that runs my Zabbix & Loki instances Vignere after the creator of the Vignere Cipher, hence the funky photo in Discord. Anyways, Vignere complained about my server using up its entire disc for all of my containers. Frustrating, but not a big deal since I'm using LXD under the hood.
Fine, I'll take my lumps. Took down all of my sites briefly, expanding the underlying ZFS sparse file, and brought the world back up. No harm no foul, just growing pains. But of course, that really wasn't the issue. I was inundated with more alerts. Suddenly I was seeing my Gitea instance grow to consume the entire disc every single day, easily generating 20-30G of data each day. Super frustrating, and enough information on the internet says that Gitea just does this and doesn't enable repo archive cleanup by default, so that must be it. I happily go and setup some aggressive cleanup tasks thinking my problems are over. Maybe I shouldn't have setup a self-hosted git forge and just stuck with Gitlab or Github.
But no, not at all, this thin veneer of a fix rapidly crumbled under the sudden and aggressive uptick in web traffic I started seeing. Suddenly it wasn't just disc usage, I was getting inundated with CPU and Memory alerts from my poor server. I couldn't git pull or push to my Gitea. Hell my weechat client couldn't even stay connected. Everything ground to a halt for a bit. But by the time I could get away from work, or the kids, and pull out my computer to dig into it the problem had stopped. I could access everything. Sysstat and Zabbix told me that the resource utilization issues were real, but I couldn't exactly tell why from just that.
This is however, why I keep an out of band monitoring system in the first place. I need to be able to look at historic metrics to see what "normal" looks like. Otherwise it's all just guesswork. And boy did Zabbix have a story to tell me. To get a clear understanding of what I mean, lets take a quick look at the full dashboard from when I redid my Zabbix server after it failed earlier this year. Pew pew flashy graphs right? The important one here is the nginx requests and network throughput chart in the bottom left hand corner of the dashboard. Note that that's what "normal" traffic looks like for my tiny part of the internet.
And this, dear reader, is what the same graph looks like after LC was laid siege to. Massive difference right? And not a fun one either. On average I was seeing 8 requests per second come into nginx across a one month period. It's not a lot, but once again, this is just a tiny server hosting a tiny part of the interne

data.title: Triangle splatting: radiance fields represented by triangles
data.author: ath92
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种名为"Triangle Splatting"的方法，用于实时渲染光影场（radiance field），通过使用三角形来表示场景，实现了高质量的新视角合成和快速渲染。相比于基于2D或3D高斯函数的方法，Triangle Splatting能够更好地保留锐利的边缘和细节，避免模糊。该方法使用可微渲染器，通过优化三角形的顶点、颜色、透明度和光滑参数来实现高效渲染。实验表明，该方法在视觉质量、收敛速度和渲染效率上均优于现有方法，并在Mip-NeRF360数据集上取得了出色的表现。此外，三角形表示简单、兼容现有图形硬件，并能与经典计算机图形学和现代可微渲染框架结合，实现了高效的网格优化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：三角形溅射（triangle splatting）技术在图形渲染中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• praveen9920认为，三角形与底层几何对齐并共享一致方向，这种方法与简单地将高斯函数替换为三角形不同，具有创新性，期待在传统渲染管道中的应用。
• rossant通过实际渲染测试，验证了该技术在GPU渲染库中的效果，认为其渲染速度快且效果好，但使用的是标准3D光栅化技术。
• sorenjan持怀疑态度，认为三角形溅射技术是一种权宜之计，现实世界更多是体积表示，而非三角形云或高斯斑点。虽然该技术在视觉效果上表现不错，但其不优雅，且可能只是为了在GPU上高效渲染。
• porphyra支持该技术，认为这是高斯溅射的自然演进，GPU原生支持三角形渲染，并可通过优化使其在渲染管线中更高效。
• jplusequalt对高斯溅射的应用场景和目的不明确，希望了解其解决的问题及未来发展方向。
• helloplanets提出是否可以通过额外处理步骤，将该技术转换为更具风格化的低多边形效果。
• ToJans建议使用三角锥代替三角形，以实现全3D表示。
• maytc和dsp_person等对该技术的高帧率和三角形回归表示兴奋和支持。
• ipunchghosts认为自编码器输出此类溅射表示，可能在特征表示上更优，并适用于下游任务。

补充讨论：
• 作者署名顺序在不同来源中不一致，引起qwertox的困惑。
• adastra22和meindnoch等对“splat”一词不熟悉，表明图形编程中新术语或技术的出现。

争议焦点：
• 三角形溅射技术是否为权宜之计，及其在真实场景表示中的优劣。
• 该技术是否只是为了在GPU上高效渲染，而非更准确的现实世界表示。

总结：讨论围绕三角形溅射技术的实现效果、应用场景及未来发展展开，参与者对其创新性、实用性和技术细节有不同看法。

Triangle Splatting achieves high-quality novel view synthesis and fast rendering by representing scenes with triangles.
In contrast, the inherent softness of Gaussian primitives often leads to blurring and a loss of fine details, for example, beneath the bench or at the room’s door, whereas Triangle Splatting preserves sharp edges and accurately captures fine details.
Abstract
The field of computer graphics was revolutionized by models such as Neural Radiance Fields and 3D Gaussian Splatting, displacing triangles as the dominant representation for photogrammetry. In this paper, we argue for
a triangle come back.
We develop a differentiable renderer that directly optimizes triangles via end-to-end gradients. We achieve this by rendering each triangle as differentiable splats, combining the efficiency of triangles with the adaptive density of representations based on independent primitives. Compared to popular 2D and 3D Gaussian Splatting methods, our approach achieves higher visual fidelity, faster convergence, and increased rendering throughput. On the Mip-NeRF360 dataset, our method outperforms concurrent non-volumetric primitives in visual fidelity and achieves higher perceptual quality than the state-of-the-art Zip-NeRF on indoor scenes.
Triangles are
simple
,
compatible
with standard graphics stacks and GPU hardware, and
highly efficient
: for the Garden scene, we achieve over 2,400 FPS at 1280×720 resolution using an off-the-shelf mesh renderer. These results highlight the efficiency and effectiveness of triangle-based representations for high-quality novel view synthesis. Triangles bring us closer to mesh-based optimization by combining classical computer graphics with modern differentiable rendering frameworks.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Methodology
Our rendering pipeline uses
3D triangles
as primitives, each defined by three learnable 3D vertices, color, opacity, and a smoothness parameter \( \sigma \). The triangles are projected onto the image plane using a standard pinhole camera model with known intrinsics and extrinsics.
Instead of binary masks, we introduce a
smooth window function
that softly modulates the triangle's influence across pixels. This function is derived from the 2D
signed distance field (SDF)
of the triangle, which measures the distance from a pixel \( \mathbf{p} \) to the triangle’s edges.
The signed distance field \( \phi(\mathbf{p}) \) is defined as the maximum of three half-plane distances:
\( \phi(\mathbf{p}) = \max\bigl(L_1(\mathbf{p}),\,L_2(\mathbf{p}),\,L_3(\mathbf{p})\bigr) \)
where each half-space function is defined as:
\( L_i(\mathbf{p}) = \mathbf{n}_i \cdot \mathbf{p} + d_i \)
with \( \mathbf{n}_i \) denoting the outward-facing unit normal of the \( i \)-th edge, and \( d_i \) its signed offset from the origin.
The final
window function
is:
\( I(\mathbf{p}) = \mathrm{ReLU}\Bigl(\tfrac{\phi(\mathbf{p})}{\phi(\mathbf{s})}\Bigr)^\sigma \)
where \( \mathbf{s} \) is the triangle’s incenter, i.e., the point where \( \phi \) is minimized. This function satisfies:
Maximum opacity at the triangle incenter
Zero influence at and beyond the triangle boundary
Adjustable sharpness via the parameter \( \sigma \)
The figure above illustrates how the window function behaves in 1D and 2D. As \( \sigma \to 0 \), the function approximates a binary triangle mask. As \( \sigma \) increases, the transition becomes smoother, and in the limit \( \sigma \to \infty \), it becomes a delta function centered at \( \mathbf{s} \).
To render an image, we accumulate contributions from all projected triangles using
alpha blending
in
front-to-back depth order
. Since all steps are differentiable, we can optimize the triangle parameters using gradient-based learning.

44132744.article_summary: 本文提出了一种名为"Triangle Splatting"的方法，用于实时渲染光影场（radiance field），通过使用三角形来表示场景，实现了高质量的新视角合成和快速渲染。相比于基于2D或3D高斯函数的方法，Triangle Splatting能够更好地保留锐利的边缘和细节，避免模糊。该方法使用可微渲染器，通过优化三角形的顶点、颜色、透明度和光滑参数来实现高效渲染。实验表明，该方法在视觉质量、收敛速度和渲染效率上均优于现有方法，并在Mip-NeRF360数据集上取得了出色的表现。此外，三角形表示简单、兼容现有图形硬件，并能与经典计算机图形学和现代可微渲染框架结合，实现了高效的网格优化。

data.title: LFSR CPU Running Forth
data.author: izabera
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了使用线性反馈移位寄存器（LFSR）作为程序计数器的CPU实现，该项目基于VHDL语言，面向FPGA。与传统程序计数器相比，LFSR可以节省逻辑门数量，特别适用于7400系列IC或手动布局晶体管的场景。项目包含一个完整的Forth解释器，目前在仿真中运行成功，输出启动消息"eForth 3.3"并接受输入。该CPU资源占用小，运行频率可达151.768MHz，使用少量FPGA资源。项目提供构建指南，通过GHDL进行仿真，使用Xilinx ISE 14.7进行FPGA合成。CPU为累加器架构，指令长度16位，程序计数器由8位LFSR驱动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LFSR（线性反馈移位寄存器）在处理器中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **howerj**：认为这个处理器是一个非常小众的工具，实际应用价值不大。他主要是为了探索可能性并展示其成果，同时在寻找合同工作。
• **jsd1982**：担心使用LFSR-PC会使汇编器/编译器在发出带有目标PC偏移的分支指令时变得更加困难。例如，计算两个指令之外的偏移量需要使用`lfsr(lfsr(pc))`，可能会导致差一错误。
• **tyrellj**：对LFSR等概念不熟悉，感到困惑，并提到自己缺乏硬件/电子课程的背景知识。同时提到了其他OISC（单指令集计算机）的例子，如Subleq。
• **artemonster**：分享了自己在继电器CPU中使用LFSR-PC技巧的经验，通过这种方式节省了大量的继电器，只用了3个继电器来实现3个XOR门。
• **kragen**：认为LFSR-PC处理器非常酷，并提供了历史上使用LFSR-PC的例子，如TMS 1000和Atari 2600。他还讨论了LFSR-PC在条件跳转指令中避免地址字段的可能性，并提出了使用LFSR可能带来的碰撞问题及其解决方案（如插入NOP指令）。他还提到了TMS 1000的多页ROM设计及其对分支指令的影响。

补充讨论：
• **历史背景**：kragen提供了TMS 1000和Atari 2600等历史上的LFSR-PC应用实例，并进一步探讨了LFSR在其他领域（如音调生成和DTMF音频生成）的应用。
• **技术细节**：详细讨论了LFSR-PC的实现细节，包括如何通过补码或增量操作实现远距离地址跳转，以及TMS 1000的多页ROM设计如何影响程序计数器的工作方式。
• **实际应用**：howerj和artemonster分享了他们在实际项目中使用LFSR-PC的经验，提供了实际应用中的具体例子和技巧。

争议焦点：
• 使用LFSR-PC是否会增加汇编器/编译器的复杂性，特别是发出分支指令时的偏移量计算问题（jsd1982的观点）。
• LFSR-PC在实际应用中的价值和效率问题，howerj认为其应用价值不大，而kragen提供了历史上成功的应用实例，显示其在特定场景下的潜在价值。

LFSR CPU running Forth
Author: Richard James Howe
License: 0BSD / Public Domain
Email:
mailto:howe.r.j.89@gmail.com
Repo:
https://github.com/howerj/lfsr-vhdl
This project contains a CPU written in
VHDL
for an
FPGA
using a Linear Feedback Shift
Register (
LFSR
) instead of a Program Counter, this was sometimes done to save space as
a
LFSR
requires fewer gates than an adder, however on an FPGA it will make very
little difference as the units that make an FPGA (Slices/Configurable Logic
Blocks) have carry chains in them. The saving would perhaps be more apparent if
making the system out of
7400
series ICs, or if laying transistors out by hand.
See
https://github.com/howerj/lfsr
for more information.
The system contains a fully working
Forth
interpreter.
The project currently works in simulation (it outputs the startup message
"eForth 3.3" with a new line) and accepts input (try typing "words" when the
simulation in
GHDL
is running).
Here is an example session of the simulator running:
And the VHDL running under GHDL for a limited number of cycles:
CPU Resource Utilization
The system runs can run at 151.768MHz (on a Spartan-6) according to the timing
report. The CPU itself is quite small, here is a cut-down report on the
resources consumed for commit
7dc4c9b7e03082364b09540bb2d97105d2858d0b
:
+------------------------------------------------------------+
| Module     | Slices | Slice Reg | LUTs  | BRAM/FIFO | BUFG |
+------------------------------------------------------------+
| top/       | 3/53   | 9/105     | 1/151 | 0/8       | 1/1  |
| +system    | 0/27   | 0/47      | 0/85  | 0/8       | 0/0  |
| ++bram     | 0/0    | 0/0       | 0/0   | 8/8       | 0/0  |
| ++cpu      | 27/27  | 47/47     | 85/85 | 0/0       | 0/0  |
| +uart_rx_0 | 12/12  | 24/24     | 39/39 | 0/0       | 0/0  |
| +uart_tx_0 | 11/11  | 25/25     | 26/26 | 0/0       | 0/0  |
+------------------------------------------------------------+
No LUTRAM/BUFIO/DSP48A1/BUFR/DCM/PLL_ADV used
The above is indicative only as the actual resources used may vary from
commit to commit, but also because of the tool chain and FPGA targeted.
Even given that though it is clear that this system is
small
. The CPU
only occupies 27 slices, which is only a little larger than the bit-serial
CPU available at
https://github.com/howerj/bit-serial
, and this 16-bit CPU
is
much
faster.
Building
To build you will need
make
. To make the C Virtual Machine you will need a C
compiler of your choosing.
To run the C VM type:
make run
You should be greeted by the message
eforth 3.3
. Type
bye
and hit
ENTER
to quit (
CTRL-D
will not work, this is not a bug). Type
words
for a list of
defined Forth words. An example session:
: ahoy cr ." GOODBYE, CRUEL WORLD!" cr ;
ahoy
2 2 + . cr
bye
This is not a Forth tutorial. For a Forth tutorial look elsewhere. Try "the
internet". I am sure they have something.
Making the simulation requires
GHDL
:
make simulation
There is a configuration file for the simulation in the file
tb.cfg
that
allows changing many test bench parameters without recompiling the test bench.
GHDL also allows you to set generics via the command line, which is done in the
makefile
. For example
make simulation DEBUG=2
sets the top level debug
generic to
2
, bear in mind when changing the generics in
tb.vhd
that the
makefile
can override these constants!
To build for an FPGA you will need
Xilinx ISE 14.7
:
make synthesis implementation bitfile
The system has not been tested on an FPGA at the moment. If you have any luck,
let me know.
Instruction Set and System Design
A short summary of the instruction set and design:
The machine is an accumulator based machine.
All instructions are 16-bits in length.
The top four bits determine the instruction.
The lowest four bits are the operand parameter.
Addresses are in number of 16-bit cells, not bytes.
The program counter is 8-bits in size and is advanced with a LFSR.
The top most bit determined whether the operand is used directly or
whether or it loaded first.
The instruction set has been carefully chosen so that it
should be very simple to implement in a

data.title: Is “The Phoenician Scheme” Wes Anderson's Most Emotional Film?
data.author: prismatic
data.article_summary:
韦斯·安德森的新片《腓尼基方案》是一部充满幽默的喜剧，但故事本身却颇为沉重，讲述了一个富有实业家试图实现宏大基建项目的过程。影片延续了安德森标志性的精致布景、对称构图和紧凑复杂的情节，同时也是一部充满打斗和追逐的暴力电影。与《布达佩斯大饭店》及之后作品的嵌套叙事不同，本片情节相对简单，集中跟随主角的行动。

故事聚焦于一个有趣但恶劣的男人安托瓦内·科尔达（本尼西奥·德尔·托罗饰），他是一位毫无顾忌的商业巨头。在1950年至1951年间，他试图推动一个涉及运河、隧道、铁路和水库的腓尼基国家项目，不惜使用奴隶劳工。尽管面临美国特工、国际财团和革命者的威胁，他依然冷酷无情。

影片通过科尔达与女儿利瑟尔（米娅·瑟普莱顿饰）及同父异母兄弟努巴（本尼迪克特·康伯巴奇饰）的关系，展现了家庭内部的复杂情感。安德森以精美的设计和情感张力，讲述了一个无情商人为了赢得虔诚女儿的爱而不惜一切的悲剧故事。
